title: MDN-VJEPA: Multimodal Probabilistic Joint-Embedding World Models
summary: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) learn world models by predicting future representations rather than reconstructing observations. Variational JEPA (VJEPA) gives this prediction probabilistic semantics and permits flexible conditional predictive families. We propose MDN-VJEPA, a multimodal probabilistic JEPA that instantiates the latent predictor as a mixture density network (MDN), representing future states with a Gaussian mixture whose components encode alternative futures, their probabilities, and within-mode uncertainty. For sequential prediction, we address two additional structural requirements: multi-modal futures should remain temporally coherent across a trajectory, and predictive beliefs should remain consistent when propagated to the same horizon through different temporal path compositions, as motivated by the Chapman--Kolmogorov equation. Together, these considerations define a three-level hierarchy of multimodal prediction, coherent multimodal trajectories, and compositionally consistent multimodal dynamics. Controlled experiments show that MDN-VJEPA closely recovers known branching predictive laws, that retaining the complete multimodal belief rather than its conditional mean can lead to materially different and substantially better planning decisions under branching futures, and that trajectory-level coupling and distributional consistency improve temporal coherence and multi-horizon agreement. These results support a simple principle: a probabilistic JEPA should preserve not only how uncertain the future is, but which distinct futures constitute that uncertainty, how they form coherent trajectories, and how those beliefs compose through time.

title: LACRM: LLM-Guided Mining of Directed Advertiser Competition Relationships in E-Commerce Advertising
summary: In e-commerce advertising, ad platforms typically fail to model the externalities among advertisers when making optimization decisions: an advertiser's actual performance is largely shaped by rivals competing for the same users; these rivals typically operate in overlapping product categories and at comparable budget scales. However, capturing this rivalry as an explicit, reusable signal is challenging because it is directed, multi-faceted, and partially observable. Existing paradigms such as interaction graphs, taxonomy rules, and single-embedding models do not fully capture these properties. In this paper, we propose LACRM (LLM-driven Advertiser Competition Relationship Mining), a novel framework that constructs directed competition graphs with continuous edge intensities via a three-stage pipeline. LACRM moves beyond symmetric similarity through LLM-driven role-separated profiling, which enables asymmetric multi-route retrieval to uncover both realized and latent rivals. The framework further incorporates listwise learning-to-rank aligned with temporal auction behavior to accurately model directed competition intensity. In offline retrieval experiments on an industrial benchmark, LACRM outperforms strong directed GNN baselines and ablation variants. Multi-LLM and human studies provide complementary evidence that the recovered latent rivals reflect meaningful market competition rather than merely model-generated artifacts. In production A/B tests, LACRM-guided bidding and incentive allocation increase advertising revenue by 1.73% and 1.14%, respectively. The results demonstrate the practical value of explicit competition modeling in large-scale advertising systems.

title: MRFlow: Mechanism-Structured Residual Flow Matching for Virtual Cell Perturbation Prediction
summary: Predicting cellular responses to chemical and genetic perturbations is a central test for AI virtual cells, yet many single-cell models reduce each condition to an average expression shift. This target is misaligned with perturbation biology: rare states, resistant subpopulations, and context-dependent effect sizes may coexist under the same intervention. MRFlow treats virtual-cell prediction as conditional transport between empirical single-cell measures. Control and perturbed cells are embedded in a variational latent state space, greedy low-cost supervision is constructed over detached minibatch states, and a conditional flow-matching vector field transports control populations toward perturbed populations. The field decomposes into a mechanism-structured affine dictionary, which recombines shared latent response operators with a low-rank condition-specific correction, and a spectrally controlled residual field for nonlinear cell-level variation. Genetic perturbations are encoded through a regulatory-graph GCN, chemical perturbations through Morgan fingerprints, and both enter the same conditional dynamics interface. Across eight gene and drug perturbation benchmarks, MRFlow attains the highest composite score while preserving competitive raw performance on differential-expression and distributional metrics. The results support latent distribution transport as a principled and empirically effective formulation for perturbation-aware virtual cell modeling.

title: PRIME: Frequency-Aware Unified Pruning and Merging for MoE Compression
summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have emerged as an effective paradigm for scaling large language models, yet their massive parameter footprint poses severe memory challenges for deployment. Existing compression methods typically treat expert pruning and merging as disjoint operations and rely on greedy heuristics, often leading to irreversible information loss or representational pollution. In this paper, we propose PRIME, a unified optimization framework for MoE compression via adaptive PRunIng and MErging. PRIME casts the discrete prune-merge assignment step as a global Integer Linear Programming over a frequency-weighted surrogate objective, jointly selecting pruning and merging decisions while accounting for expert usage. We motivate the frequency-aware objective through an error-bound analysis under fixed representative assignments, and show that the formulation favors high-frequency experts as centroids, promoting routing stability. Extensive experiments on Qwen3-30B-A3B and Qwen3.5-122B-A10B demonstrate that PRIME achieves strong accuracy retention across knowledge, coding, math, and long-context tasks, while serving benchmarks of merged models quantify the memory and throughput benefits of expert compression in vLLM.

title: Semantic Edge-Cloud Communication for Real-Time Urban Traffic Digital Twins
comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, accepted to IEEE Global Communications (Globecom) Conference, 2026
summary: Urban traffic systems are becoming increasingly complex, demanding real-time traffic perception, proactive collision prediction, and intelligent management to improve safety and reduce congestion. Although AI-driven traffic management has shown strong promise, its success relies on diverse, high-quality data spanning critical scenarios such as collisions, near-collisions, and traffic rule violations. Digital twins offer a powerful solution by enabling synchronized virtual replicas of physical traffic environments for real-time monitoring, collision prediction, traffic-flow optimization, and diverse realistic scenario generation. However, continuously synchronizing a high-fidelity urban traffic digital twin through edge surveillance cameras requires substantial edge-cloud communication, and transmitting raw video streams leads to severe bandwidth and latency constraints. To overcome this challenge, this paper proposes a semantic communication-based edge-cloud framework for real-time urban traffic digital twin applications. By leveraging edge intelligence to extract and transmit only task-relevant semantic traffic information instead of full video feeds, the proposed framework significantly reduces communication overhead while preserving the essential dynamics needed for accurate real-time digital twin reconstruction. Experimental results demonstrate more than 99% transmission savings and an average trajectory reconstruction error of only 0.12 m, confirming the proposed framework as an effective, scalable, and low-latency solution for AI-enabled urban traffic digital twin applications.

title: Mutual Coupling and Visibility Effects in 2D Holographic Curvature-Reconfigurable Apertures
summary: Holographic multiple-input multiple-output arrays provide high spatial resolution and flexible wavefront control, but curved or conformal deployments jointly introduce curvature, mutual coupling (MC), and direction-dependent visibility. This paper studies a two-dimensional (2D) holographic curvaturereconfigurable aperture (HoloCuRA). A geometry-based model characterizes element positions, steering, and spatial correlation, while an impedance-based coupling matrix and a visibility vector capture electromagnetic interactions and shadowing. Relative directivity and spectral efficiency are evaluated versus curvature. Results show that MC mainly reshapes local directivity fluctuations, whereas visibility dominates the global pattern and spectral-efficiency variation under both isotropic scattering and CDL-A channels.

title: WZIP and WLZ4: LZ77 Codecs with Match-Length-Dependent Sliding Windows
comment: 10 pages, 5 tables, 2 figures. Submitted to the 2027 Data Compression Conference (DCC). Source code: https://github.com/icodywu/WZIP (release v1.0.0). Distinct from arXiv:2610.06530, which analyzes length-dependent window schedules in theory; this paper presents two complete codecs, their formats, parser and decoders, and measurements against LZ4, Zstandard, Brotli and xz
summary: An LZ77 codec bounds every match by one sliding window, trading cheap offsets for short matches against reach for long ones. Match-length-dependent windows refine this trade-off: each match length has its own window, and the decoder infers the offset range from the decoded length. We present two such codecs: WLZ4, a byte-aligned LZ4-class format with one-byte and flagged offsets, and WZIP, an entropy-coded Zstandard-class format. Each block begins with its decoded length, from which WZIP derives its widest window and a decoder sizes its output. LZ4 blocks may expand incompressible input by 0.4%; WLZ4 adds at most 15 bytes, WZIP 2. We describe the formats, threaded match finders, decoders and parser. On Silesia, WLZ4 reaches a ratio up to 16% above LZ4HC's, decoding more slowly, and WZIP exceeds Zstandard 22's ratio while its trusted decoder runs at 91% of Zstandard's speed (87% checked; on enwik9, about as fast).

title: Large-Scale Data Center Integration in Power Systems: Uncertainty and Multi-Scale Variation
comment: Accepted for publication in Proceedings of the IEEE. Copyright 2026 IEEE. Personal use of this material is permitted. Permission from IEEE must be obtained for all other uses
summary:
Hyperscale artificial intelligence (AI) data centers are emerging as a structurally new class of electricity demand. Unlike conventional loads, they materialize as spatially concentrated, transmission-level point loads with rapid deployment timelines and converter-dominated dynamics. Their integration is governed by two defining properties: forecast uncertainty in load realization and multi-scale temporal variation spanning sub-seconds to planning horizons.
  We develop a unified framework that links reliability and affordability to these dimensions through a four-quadrant structure: (reliability, affordability) $\times$ (uncertainty, variation), which integrates probabilistic resource adequacy, generation and transmission expansion, operational security, and market design.
  Measured traces from a public generative-AI workload dataset show strongly tonal GPU power spectra rather than smooth broadband behavior: harmonic combs at the training-step cadence, and a distinct sub-second periodicity in inference. Across these traces the dominant variance band shifts with workload type (seconds for training and offline inference; tens of seconds and longer for online inference). We report this as a characterization of the measured workloads rather than a universal signature, and take it to indicate that such loads warrant a spectral description rather than a peak-demand one. These signatures directly affect reserve requirements, ramping products, voltage stability, ride-through performance, and harmonic interactions in converter-rich grids.
  Taken together, the analytical framework and empirical results establish a system-level basis for assessing the reliability and cost implications of large AI data center integration across planning and operational horizons.

title: Argos: A Multi-Tenant SaaS Architecture for Distributed Edge Security Orchestration
summary: The growing adoption of distributed edge devices for security auditing and operational monitoring exposes limitations in lightweight control mechanisms traditionally used to manage such nodes. While commercial Command-and-Control (C2) platforms offer advanced orchestration features, their licensing constraints, operational complexity, and proprietary nature limit accessibility for small and medium-sized enterprises and research environments. This paper presents Argos, a multi-tenant SaaS C2 architecture designed for transparent, automated, and long-term orchestration of distributed edge devices. The framework implements a structured control plane with role-based access control (RBAC), tenant isolation, persistent task management, and cron-based workflow automation. Unlike operator-driven or stateless execution models, Argos enables scheduled and autonomous coordination of security tasks across heterogeneous environments. To formally substantiate its isolation guarantees, the platform is modeled through a set-theoretic authorization framework, and a tenant non-interference property is proven. The proposed architecture was evaluated across three geographically distributed edge devices, executing 810 automated tasks mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques. Results demonstrate a global failure rate of 3.33% (95% Wilson confidence interval: [2.30%, 4.81%]) with no statistically significant difference across ARM and x86 architectures (\c{hi} 2 = 1.55, p = 0.21), and stable operation under heterogeneous latency conditions, including intercontinental deployments. To ensure scientific transparency and reproducibility, the evaluation methodology, sanitized datasets, and statistical scripts have been made publicly available in an open-source repository.

title: DoSA: Dots Sparse Attention
summary: Sparse attention visits few keys, yet finding them can still require scoring every key with every indexer head. We introduce DoSA (Dots Sparse Attention), a lossless method for making this computation conditional while preserving exact token selection. Its central observation is that Top-K selection requires sufficient evidence to reject a candidate, not necessarily its full score. A seed set supplies a lower bound on the winning threshold. Nonnegative head projections and joint residual bounds upper-bound positive contributions, while activation-informed aggregation bounds the magnitude subtracted by negative heads. The certificate directs full scoring toward candidates that remain eligible; exact-score filtering further reduces writeback and selection work. We establish the certificate and its exact-selection conditions, and analyze how geometry and selection margins govern its effectiveness. Our GPU implementation accelerates the complete Indexer by up to 2.74 times over SGLang and 1.69 times over LiteTopK across English, Chinese, and code workloads. End-to-end evaluation on GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V3.2 achieves up to 1.94 times and 1.50 times time-to-first-token speedups over the two baselines, respectively.

title: An Availability Management Framework for Microservice-Based Safety-Critical CIoT Systems: Architecture and End-to-End Evaluation
summary: Safety-critical Cellular Internet of Things (CIoT) systems increasingly rely on microservice architectures orchestrated across heterogeneous edge and cloud platforms. Although this paradigm improves modularity and scalability, the fault-tolerance mechanisms of contemporary orchestration platforms remain predominantly reactive, i.e., failed components are restarted or rescheduled only after an outage has already occurred. Such recovery can produce multi-second End to End Service Outage Time (E2E SOT), which can grow further under container restart backoff. This paper proposes an Availability Management Framework (AMF), a generic monitor-predict-recover loop that complements reactive recovery with machine learning-based anomaly detection and make-before-break switchover to a standby replica. Candidate ML models are evaluated offline under three protocols, including a change of operating regime, in order to select a model for live deployment. AMF is instantiated and evaluated on a three-tier tele-operated driving (ToD) testbed under a staged resource-exhaustion scenario. Relative to Kubernetes-only recovery, AMF completes switchover during the anomaly window, reduces E2E SOT, and avoids the tens-of-seconds outages associated with repeated in-place restarts under backoff. On this non-real-time testbed, residual E2E SOT lies inside healthy-path jitter and is therefore limited by path timing rather than by lateness of the recovery decision. The paper whows that coupling a validated ML based anomaly detector with proactive switchover can remove restart- and backoff-dominated outage from a critical path.

title: UAV SAR Imaging via Diffusion Posterior Sampling under Non-Ideal Motion in ISAC Systems
summary: Unmanned aerial vehicle-enabled synthetic aperture radar (SAR) offers significant potential for providing communication services to ground users while sensing the surrounding environment in low-altitude integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. However, its practical deployment is challenged by known non-ULM trajectories and unknown position errors, which violate conventional SAR assumptions and cause severe image defocusing. We address these non-ideal impacts by formulating the ISAC SAR imaging as an exact linear inverse problem to accurately model arbitrary trajectories with multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency division multiplexing waveforms. Based on this formulation, we develop a diffusion posterior sampling (DPS)-based super-resolution SAR framework, where a pre-trained diffusion model provides a data-driven image prior and the exact physical model enforces measurement consistency during posterior inference. The inference process is further accelerated for practical implementation. For unknown position errors, we develop a joint iterative DPS and motion compensation (MoCo) optimization algorithm with discrete cosine transform reparameterization and coarse-to-fine spectral scheduling. Simulations demonstrate that our framework achieves high-accuracy reconstruction across diverse trajectories and remarkable super-resolution, maintaining greater than 21.3 dB peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) even under half physical resolution truncation. Under unknown motion errors, the joint DPS and MoCo algorithm achieves 23.65 dB PSNR with a residual position-error estimation error of 0.19 cm.

title: The weight enumerators of irreducible cyclic codes of length $2^\ell$
summary: Using the spectral relation between irreducible cyclic codes (ICC) and generalized Paley (GP) graphs recently found by the authors, we study the weight distribution of irreducible cyclic codes of length $2^\ell$, $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$. These codes were previously studied by Sharma, Bakshi and Raka, who divided them into two families (each having two cases). First we characterize the GP-graphs spectrally related to these families of ICCs: they are complete, semiprimitive, Hamming, or Cartesian products of semiprimitive GP-graphs. We then compute the spectrum of these graphs and hence, by the mentioned spectral relation we finally obtain neat explicit expressions for the weight enumerators of all the irreducible cyclic codes of length $2^\ell$ with $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$.

title: Zero-Crossing Time Lower Bounds for the Homogeneous Super-Twisting Algorithm
summary: High-frequency switching and chattering are well-known problems in sliding-mode control. Although the super-twisting algorithm produces a continuous control input, the sliding variable may still cross zero repeatedly near the sliding manifold. This paper studies how fast these crossings can occur and whether they can accumulate in finite time for the scalar homogeneous super-twisting algorithm. Two lower bounds on the time required to return to zero are derived, together with a bound on the time needed to complete a full excursion. These results give minimum separation times and upper bounds on the number of crossings associated with excursions above a prescribed amplitude. Although zero crossings may accumulate in finite time, the amplitudes of the complete excursions considered here must vanish and satisfy a summability condition. Thus, crossings associated with excursions above any prescribed nonzero amplitude cannot accumulate in finite time. When the perturbation-rate bound is zero, the estimates recover the scaling imposed by homogeneity. For the classical super-twisting algorithm, the square-root scaling also holds for nonzero perturbation-rate bounds. Numerical simulations illustrate the results.

title: Symmetric Cryptography via Dirichlet Convolution
summary:
We discuss a new symmetric-key cipher for digital data encryption. Its implementation is fast, memory efficient, and resilient against classical, AI-assisted, and quantum attacks.
  Let $x$, $k$, and $c$ be elements of a finite abelian group $G$ with operation $+$ and neutral element $0$. Suppose one is given ciphertext $c=x+k$. Retrieving the plaintext $x=c-k$ from the ciphertext is trivial when the key $k$ is known. Without the key, however, recovering $x$ amounts to a blind search. Even if an efficient criterion were available for identifying the plaintext among all group elements, the average number of trials would remain prohibitively large when the group is sufficiently large. The challenge in constructing a practical cryptosystem is therefore to identify a sufficiently rich group $G$, together with efficient algorithms that enable an immersion of \emph{real digital data} into $G$ and efficient evaluation of the group operations.
  The proposed cipher is based on generalized Dirichlet convolution over finite fields. We investigate its security against plaintext attacks from an information-theoretic perspective. The nonlocal structure of Dirichlet convolution naturally permits plaintext salting, providing protection against plaintext attacks while allowing controlled key reuse. We establish perfect masking properties over finite fields and prove that the resulting cipher achieves information-theoretic security under key reuse when the underlying arithmetic is carried out in $\mathbb{F}_p$ with $p>2$. For arithmetic over $\mathbb{F}_2$, some information leakage remains, leading to a finite key-reuse budget.

title: Predict Before You Modify: Learning Improvement Dynamics for Self-Evolving Agents
summary: Self-evolving agents improve through repeated cycles of modification and evaluation. However, existing methods receive feedback on modifications only after costly evaluations, and aggregate scores may obscure distinctions between failures that require different repairs. We introduce predictive self-evolution through an editable Improvement Dynamics Model (IDM). Before evaluation, the IDM predicts task-level outcomes of a proposed modification and guides an optional revision. After evaluation, past modifications and their observed outcomes are used to improve the IDM, allowing predictive knowledge to accumulate across generations. The system can thus improve how it solves tasks, proposes modifications, and predicts their effects. Building on HyperAgents, we evaluate this approach across multilingual coding, paper review, robotics reward design, and Olympiad-level mathematical grading. Our approach outperforms HyperAgents across all four domains, with up to 46% higher average performance over generations. Gains also persist under matched token budgets that include both agent evolution and task evaluation, and extend to held-out tasks. Forecast accuracy improves as the IDM evolves, and the learned predictive knowledge transfers to improve evolution in a new domain.

title: Harvesting-Aware Routing for Low-Latency Reliable Transmission in Interference-Powered Networks
summary: We consider a multi-hop wireless network where energy-harvesting nodes rely solely on ambient radio-frequency interference as their power source. The goal is to deliver a packet from source to destination with minimum latency while guaranteeing a target end-to-end outage probability under Rayleigh fading. This gives rise to a joint routing and power allocation problem in which interference plays a dual role: it provides harvestable energy, but also impairs link reliability. We first transform the intricate, multiplicative end-to-end outage constraint into an additive form. Then, we propose two optimal algorithms. The first, HOPE, minimizes the bottleneck harvesting latency, i.e., the longest energy-accumulation time along the path, by reducing the problem to a least-cost path computation on a graph with interference-aware link weights. The second, THOPE, extends the objective to total end-to-end latency, adding the cumulative transmission delay, and likewise admits a closed-form least-cost path solution. Both algorithms are solved in polynomial time via Dijkstra's algorithm and yield explicit expressions for the optimal transmit powers. Extensive simulations reveal that HOPE and THOPE reduce the average total latency by up to an order of magnitude compared with shortest-path and minimum-energy benchmarks, while exhibiting sharply concentrated delay distributions that are largely insensitive to interferer density.

title: Performance Evaluation of Mobile Target Sensing and Tracking Across Multiple Sensing Modes
summary: Moving extended-target sensing and tracking are studied in a beamformed PRS/OFDM ISAC framework. The target is modeled as a rigid cluster of scatterers whose Tx--target--Rx echoes coherently combine in a MIMO scattering channel. Delay, azimuth/elevation, and Doppler are estimated using PRS matched filtering with delay centroiding, single-cluster 2D-MUSIC, and FFT-based Doppler estimation, then used for independent localization and EKF-based tracking. The framework is evaluated in monostatic and bistatic modes under target-directed, receiver-directed, and omnidirectional beamforming. Simulation results show that EKF tracking reduces the aggregate 3D RMSE from 1.61 m to 1.38 m relative to independent localization. Target-directed beamforming substantially improves tracking accuracy, achieving 1.38 m RMSE compared with 5.91 m and 8.38 m for omnidirectional and receiver-directed beamforming, respectively. The results highlight the importance of target-aware beam management, delay-angle-Doppler fusion, and sensing geometry for mobile-target tracking in ISAC networks.

title: Quantum Annealing for Resource Allocation in Next-Generation Wireless Communication Networks: A QUBO Modeling Guide
comment: 16 pages, 5 figures, and 7 tables. Accepted by OJ-COMS
summary: Quantum annealing (QA) offers a physics-inspired approach for such subproblems by mapping them onto an Ising Hamiltonian, which is algebraically equivalent to a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) model executable on quantum annealers or hybrid solvers. However, their practical employment in wireless systems critically depends on the specific problem formulation, on the particular variable encoding, constraint handling, solver selection, hardware embedding, and fair benchmarking. This paper develops wireless-oriented QUBO modeling guidelines for QA-assisted resource allocation. We first present a beginner-friendly toy example in which a terrestrial-aerial resource-allocation problem with a fractional signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) maximization objective is reformulated into a two-bit QUBO via Boolean interpolation, converted into an Ising representation, and decoded back into a wireless scheduling decision. The same scheduling is applicable to UAV, aircraft, satellite, and terrestrial links in SAGIN systems. We then review the QA foundations and solver ecosystems, including binary quadratic, discrete quadratic, constrained quadratic, and hybrid models from the perspective of NG wireless optimization. Furthermore, we discuss both binary and discrete encoding, penalty-based constraint conversion, embedding overhead, solution decoding, and feasibility verification. A QUBO Compatibility Index is introduced as a lightweight diagnostic metric for assessing the associated QUBO formulation readiness, rather than a predictor of runtime or solution quality. Finally, a case study on max-min uplink power control in cell-free massive MIMO illustrates how a fairness-oriented wireless problem can be discretized, constrained, converted into the concept of a QUBO, and evaluated against classical baselines. A host of key challenges and future directions are also discussed.

title: Deep learning from a control vantage point
summary: This article offers an overview of recent developments in deep learning from a control vantage point. It reviews several classes of models including feedforward and residual neural networks, transformers, large-language models, and selective state space models while explaining how control theory plays an important role in understanding their training, properties, or architecture design. The article explains how residual neural networks can be interpreted as the discretization of a continuous-time control system thereby enabling the use of control theoretic techniques for its analysis. To illustrate the power of this bridge between control and deep learning, two technical results are discussed: 1) the ability of a residual neural network to approximate arbitrary continuous functions is a non-standard controllability problem that can be solved using geometric nonlinear control and 2) transformers, the key architectural component of most large language-models, can be seen the discretization of a consensus algorithm and thus large language-models exhibit consensus. Another point of contact between control theory and deep learning is the connection between backpropagation, the algorithm used to train neural networks, and optimal control. The article addresses how the older connection between these problems, established in the 80's using discrete-time models can be reconciled with the more recent approach using continuous-time models. Several open problems and directions for future research are discussed, including selective state-space models, a recent class of models inspired by the models used in control.

title: SAGE: Efficient Protected Vision-Language Inference on Smart Glasses
summary: Smart glasses are a promising platform for vision-language assistants, but private split inference remains expensive: protecting visual representations before transmission does not remove the cost of on-device vision encoding, wide protected tokens, or hardware-unaware execution. We present SAGE (Smart-glasses-Aware Guarded Encoding), a hardware-aware framework for efficient protected VLM inference on smart glasses. SAGE keeps raw images and unprotected visual tokens on the trusted device, reduces visual input cost, executes shape-specialized INT8 graphs, and compresses protected representations into compact 256-dimensional INT8 packets before transmission. Unlike efficiency methods optimized only for nominal model size, SAGE selects its operating point using downstream answer quality together with measured latency, memory, and thermal behavior on real Mentra Live glasses. On a matched Qwen workload, SAGE reduces glasses inference latency by 39.18%, device-sensor temperature rise by 21.91%, and protected packet size by 96.56%, while retaining 85.62% of the protected reference's relaxed utility and comparable prompted containment. Direct glasses-to-phone tests deliver all 192 packets and reduce median packet-plus-acknowledgment time from 71.3 to 10.0 ms. The compact protected interface also transfers across four additional VLM families. These results show that private wearable VLM inference must be optimized jointly across representation protection, communication, and real-device execution rather than through model compression alone.

title: Posterior Flow Matching
summary: Flow matching learns how to transport noise toward data, but its mean prediction does not directly report the endpoint uncertainty remaining at an intermediate state. This paper introduces Posterior Flow Matching (PFM), a general generative modeling framework that learns conditional velocity means and componentwise variances with a Gaussian posterior model. The same model evaluation supplies both a transport prediction and endpoint uncertainty, making posterior diagnostics available throughout generation. These learned moments support a mean-driven ordinary differential equation (ODE) and a posterior-driven stochastic differential equation (SDE), whose local noise scales adapt to the predicted uncertainty. Across image, point-cloud, molecular, and action generation, PFM improves generation quality and provides endpoint-posterior readouts throughout generation.

title: RADIUS-Assisted Companion PSK Discovery: Enabling WPA3-SAE in Externally Authenticated Multi-PSK (ePSK / MPSK / DPSK / iPSK / PPSK) Deployments
summary: Large multi-dwelling unit (MDU), student-housing and hospitality networks rarely store resident pre-shared keys (PSKs) on the access point (AP). Instead, the per-resident keys of ePSK, MPSK, DPSK, iPSK or PPSK services are held in an external RADIUS server or cloud database synchronised with the property-management system. Our earlier work, Companion-BSSID-Assisted PSK Discovery (CAPD), brought WPA3-SAE to multi-PSK networks by learning the client's PSK on a WPA2-only companion BSSID and steering the client with IEEE 802.11v to a hidden WPA2/WPA3 primary BSSID of the same SSID. CAPD assumes that the AP can test every PSK itself. This paper removes that assumption. We propose RADIUS-Assisted Companion PSK Discovery (RA-CAPD). The AP forwards the ANonce, the raw EAPOL-Key message 2 (SNonce, MIC, RSNE), the SSID, the client MAC, the BSSID and the AP MAC to the external server in RADIUS vendor-specific attributes (VSAs). The server validates the MIC against all provisioned keys, identifies the matching PSK, and returns it encrypted under the RADIUS shared secret (or a per-AP key for cloud databases), together with the unit, room or user identity and the VLAN. The AP binds the client to this PSK and identity, synchronises the binding across all APs in the domain, and moves the client to the configured profile: 802.11v-capable clients via a BSS Transition Management request, and other clients by disconnection and reconnection. On that profile, SAE-capable clients complete WPA3-SAE and WPA2-only clients complete WPA2-PSK, both with the learned key and no further search, so the companion BSSID serves only for onboarding. We present the design, attribute dictionary, algorithms, complexity and security properties, together with laboratory validation on commercial access points.

title: Efficient Multimodal Beam Prediction for Real-World 6G UAV Communications via Image-Position-Synthetic Fusion
summary: Camera-based beam selection can reduce the need for exhaustive channel measurement in highly mobile millimeter-wave UAV links, but the complementary value of visual and position-derived representations and their behavior under modality degradation require further investigation. This paper develops a staged multimodal framework for current-beam prediction using real-world UAV measurements. The proposed 32-beam classifier combines an ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNet-B3 visual encoder with two deterministic position-derived representations: an explicit Geometric-Kinematic vector and a nonlinear synthetic feature basis constructed from position. The image and synthetic representations are fused first, followed by late fusion with the geometry representation. Experiments on DeepSense 6G Scenario 23 show that Image-Synthetic fusion achieves 86.92% Top-1, 99.03% Top-3, and 99.56% Top-5 accuracy, improving Top-1 performance by 2.64 percentage points over image-only inference and outperforming the 60.71% Top-1 accuracy of synthetic-only inference. Adding the Geometric-Kinematic branch yields the highest measured performance, reaching 87.14% Top-1, 99.12% Top-3, and 99.60% Top-5 accuracy. Controlled input interventions further demonstrate complementary behavior under visual degradation and strong sensitivity to severe synthetic-input corruption. Position-derived nonlinear features provide complementary information to visual context and improve current-beam prediction in the evaluated real-world UAV setting.

title: Sequential Change Point Detection for PSK Modulation Switching
comment: 12 Pages, 5 Figures, Online change-point detection for modulation transitions using CUSUM and MOSUM detectors
summary: Transmitters in adaptive communication systems may switch their modulation scheme at an unknown time, and a receiver must detect this switch quickly without raising frequent false alarms. Existing modulation classification methods label a finite block of received data and do not provide stopping rules with controlled false-alarm and delay performance. We study the sequential detection of a switch from one phase shift keying (PSK) scheme to another over an additive white Gaussian noise channel. We build cumulative-sum (CUSUM) and moving-sum (MOSUM) detectors from the log-likelihood ratio and its low-SNR approximation. For a switch from quadrature PSK to binary PSK, we derive the moment-generating function and probability density function of the approximate statistic. We use them to relate the CUSUM threshold to the average run length to false alarm and the worst-case detection delay. For a switch between any two PSK orders, we approximate the vector of overlapping MOSUM statistics as multivariate Gaussian and obtain bounds on both measures. Monte Carlo simulations show that our derived expressions for ARL2FA and WADD closely match the empirical results across thresholds, validating the accuracy of the proposed analytical approximations and theoretical bounds.

title: Spatial-Temporal Hybrid Path Planning for Multi-UAV Methane Emission Rate Quantification
summary: Accurate emission-rate quantification of methane point sources is essential for inventory verification and leak detection. UAV-borne sensing provides high-resolution, near-source measurements, but existing quantification methods mostly follow a predefined trajectory and rely on a single UAV. Building on a source receptor matrix (SRM) estimator and empirical observability Gramian (EMGR)-based path planning, this paper proposes a spatial-temporal hybrid path planning strategy for multi-UAV methane emission rate quantification. Measurements are time-averaged, and the forward Gaussian plume model is calibrated against a filament-based plume simulator (MOABS) to reduce model mismatch. Cooperating UAVs first spread out spatially to locate the source quickly, then switch to sequentially retracing a leader trajectory with a time lag to reduce quantification variance. Simulations show that the spatial stage localizes the source markedly faster than a single-UAV baseline, the temporal stage yields the lowest variance but converges slowly, and the proposed hybrid strategy converges substantially faster than the purely temporal strategy while matching its steady-state accuracy, with a narrower error band than the purely spatial strategy. A window-length study further shows that longer time-averaging windows exhibit diminishing returns, justifying the balance between spatial coverage and temporal averaging.

title: An Empirical Case Study of Prompt Engineering Strategies for Bypassing Multi-Layer Agent Security Defenses
comment: 5 pages, 6 tables. Accepted at The 2nd Workshop on AIGC Safety from Dual Perspectives of Model and Content (WS06), IJCAI-ECAI 2026. Case study from Track 1 of the OpenClaw Security Attack and Defense Challenge
summary: The OpenClaw Security Attack and Defense Challenge evaluates AI agent robustness through a three-stage defense pipeline: skill file scanning (Stage 1), instruction safety evaluation (Stage 2), and attack trajectory scoring (Stage 3). This paper presents an empirical case study of prompt engineering strategies against these layers across 19 attack targets in Enterprise OA, E-commerce, and Smart Home scenarios. I document both successful and failed strategies, with an emphasis on the observed trade-off between instruction safety (Stage 2) and attack execution accuracy (Stage 3). The final online score is 0.2630, with 5 of 19 tasks achieving full bypass. The results suggest that multi-layer defenses, reinforced by built-in behavioral constraints, substantially limit what prompt engineering alone can achieve.

title: GameSmith: Scaling Zero-Sum Self-Play with Synthesised Games
summary: Post-training large language models (LLMs) on two-player zero-sum games provides a verifiable reward, and the gains have been shown to transfer to general reasoning. Existing pipelines, however, rely on a handful of hand-written games and on advantage estimators tied to them, so both the supply of games and the advantage estimate on a large corpus limit scaling. We present GameSmith, which scales both. An LLM synthesises games inside templates whose reward, observation, and hidden-information code is fixed. Each game is verified by seed-paired replay and by an independent re-implementation of its specification, then expanded into encoding, rule, and size variants, giving 26 new games in 29 families and 336 verified variants from the three SPIRAL templates. The model is distilled from the self-play of a larger teacher (Qwen3-32B) on these games and then trained by self-play reinforcement learning with CRAB, an advantage estimator that credits each decision against a shrinkage estimate of the expected return of its position and is defined on every variant. On Qwen3-4B-Base, distillation raises the 13-benchmark mean pass@1 from 45.5 to 62.5, above the three SPIRAL games at the same budget, and self-play with CRAB reaches 64.9. The ordering holds across models, and transfer grows with the number of game families.

title: Energy-Aware Agentic Orchestration for Multi-Site Service Deployment
comment: Accepted author manuscript for publication in the Proceedings of the 2026 IEEE Future Networks World Forum (FNWF 2026), Lisbon, Portugal, October 26-28, 2026
summary: Energy-aware orchestration across geographically distributed infrastructures is increasingly important as data centers absorb growing Artificial Intelligence (AI) workloads. However, existing approaches often exclude the energy cost of automated decision-making from system-level sustainability assessments. This paper presents an energy-aware agentic orchestration framework that treats Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning as a measurable component of the control loop. We compare single-shot tool calling, ReAct, and plan-and-execute strategies on a multi-site Kubernetes testbed spanning two European data centers and instrumented at layers ranging from power distribution units to per-pod energy attribution. Using ten natural-language orchestration intents with varying decision complexity, we show that reasoning strategy and intent complexity strongly influence graphics processing unit (GPU) energy consumption during orchestration decisions. ReAct and plan-and-execute generated executable tool calls across all evaluated intents but required multiple LLM inferences, whereas the single-shot configuration was less costly but non-actionable. Prefix caching reduced mean ReAct GPU energy consumption by 29.4%. For the evaluated lightweight workload, the infrastructure-energy changes observed within the one-second measurement window were insufficient to offset the measured GPU decision energy. These findings demonstrate the importance of accounting for reasoning overhead when assessing the sustainability of AI-native orchestration and motivate energy-budgeted selection of agent strategies.

title: Adaptive DOA Estimation With KL-Based Kernel Bandwidth Adaptation Under Impulsive Noise
summary: Direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation can degrade markedly in impulsive noise, where methods relying on Gaussian or second-order statistical assumptions are particularly susceptible to large-amplitude outliers. This paper develops an adaptive DOA estimator that employs Gaussian kernel weighting to attenuate the influence of large prediction errors while adjusting the kernel bandwidth online according to a Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence criterion. A sample-based approximation of the KL criterion yields a recursive bandwidth update that adapts the degree of outlier suppression to the observed error statistics rather than prescribing a fixed bandwidth a priori. The spatial-filter coefficients and kernel bandwidth are updated recursively, and the DOAs are recovered from the resulting spatial spectrum. Mean and mean-square analyses are developed under standard adaptive-filtering approximations to characterize the coefficient convergence and steady-state behavior. Simulation results under Gaussian-mixture impulsive noise demonstrate stable coefficient adaptation and improved DOA estimation accuracy over representative competing methods in several challenging operating regimes, with the most pronounced gains occurring at low-to-moderate signal-to-noise ratios. The results also indicate reduced sensitivity to the initial kernel bandwidth through online bandwidth adaptation.

title: Orthogonal SC-LDPC Codes for the IDS Channel
summary: We propose a coding scheme for the insertion, deletion and substitution (IDS) channel tailored to the short strands of DNA-based data storage. Instead of an inner synchronisation code, a spatially coupled LDPC (SC-LDPC) code is placed across the strands, with its coupling axis aligned to the position along the strands. Every decoded position thus becomes an anchor to synchronise the neighbouring strands. The decoding waves of the SC-LDPC code carry these anchors from both ends of the strands towards the middle. We bound the achievable rate from above by the information rate of a single strand and from below by that of a separated receiver. For strands of 100 nucleotides (the relevant regime for DNA-based data storage), our scheme outperforms a rate-matched concatenated construction.

title: Encrypted collision avoidance maneuver via variational optimization
comment: 15 pages, 1 figure, extended abstract submited to AAS/AIAA Space Flight Mechanics Meeting
summary: We propose an encrypted collision avoidance maneuver (CAM) design protocol using homomorphic encryption (HE) that enables operators to outsource CAM design to an untrusted server without revealing their private covariance. To this end, we reformulate the constrained CAM optimization as a sampling based estimation problem via a variational approach, so that the private covariance dependent terms can be efficiently evaluated under HE. The protocol requires only a single round of communication, and experiments on six real-world conjunction data messages demonstrate improved feasibility and reduced fuel consumption compared with CAMs designed using public covariance.

title: TrustPaper for forged PDF with Issuer Fingerprints
summary: Sick leave certificates are increasingly delivered as PDF files by online teleconsultation platforms, and can be altered in minutes with free editors. Generic PDF scanners report how a file was built, but cannot tell whether that construction is legitimate: an incremental update, an embedded font or a given producer string is normal for one issuer and anomalous for another. We present TrustPaper solution, an issuer aware forensic approach that combines three elements: the claimed issuer of the document, a reference fingerprint learned beforehand from genuine documents of that issuer, and an explainable combination of evidence from several forensic modules. Fingerprints are stored as versioned declarative profiles, and every anomaly keeps its observed value, expected value and triggering rule. We formalize the threat model, the fingerprint and the scoring model, and evaluate the open-source prototype on a controlled corpus documents from two issuers and six forgery techniques. With the issuer fingerprint, all forgeries made by opportunistic and metadata-aware attackers are flagged with no false positive on genuine test documents.

title: Splicing Hints into Reasoning Traces: Learning from Demonstrator Failures
summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards improves mathematical reasoning when a final answer can be checked, but a correct answer does not certify the derivation behind it, and proof problems offer no answer to check. Replacing the check with a reasoning model as an in-loop verifier faces a fundamental obstacle: the policy must already produce occasional correct attempts for any reward to exist, which it may never do at olympiad level. We instead move verification and repair out of the training loop and into offline data generation with SPLICE, a workflow in which a second model, given only a reference solution, edits a reasoning model's traces as they are generated: it verifies progress, truncates a failed trace at its last verified step, and splices in an adaptively strengthened hint until progress resumes. The resulting dataset includes repaired examples whose sampled unaided trajectory failed, with failed continuations removed and progress repeatedly checked against the reference solution. A model finetuned on SPLICE traces outperforms the same model distilled from the reasoning model's unedited traces on AIME and, under a grading protocol validated against human grades, on olympiad proofs. The trained model's own traces show a corresponding behavioral signature: at difficult points it announces a branch in the style of the spliced hints and takes riskier steps, with predictive entropy rising there and just after, a pattern absent from the model trained on unedited traces.

title: Stackelberg Game with Multi-Agent Transformer for ISRS-Aware Resource Re-optimization in Multi-Band Optical Networks
summary: The rapid expansion of generative AI is driving computing infrastructures toward interconnected AI data centers. Multi-band optical networks have become the backbone of such connectivity. To accommodate increasingly dynamic traffic demands, these networks require continual resource re-optimization to improve resource utilization and reduce service blocking. However, multi-band transmission amplifies inter-channel stimulated Raman scattering(ISRS), inducing nonlinear coupling among services. This coupling complicates re-optimization, as local adjustments perturb the global power profile, creating interdependent optimization decisions across services. Moreover, the nonlinear interactions vary with the subset of services selected for re-optimization, and inappropriate selection may reduce re-optimization effectiveness or diminish achievable benefits. To address these challenges, we propose a Stackelberg Game with Multi-Agent Transformer (SG-MAT) approach for ISRS-aware resource re-optimization. SG-MAT employs a leader-follower structure, in which the MAT-based follower models nonlinear coupling and generates coordinated channel reallocations, feeding the utilization improvements to the leader. Using this feedback, the leader identifies critical service subsets, approximating a Stackelberg equilibrium to guide global decisions and enabling consistent and efficient re-optimization. Simulation results show that SG-MAT achieves the highest utilization improvement and reduces the blocking ratio by approximately 30% under moderate traffic loads, with computational complexity comparable to benchmarks.

title: UL-Assisted Parametric CSI Feedback and Prediction for FDD Systems
comment: The paper is accepeted in GlobeCom 2026
summary: In frequency-division duplex (FDD) systems, the uplink (UL) and downlink (DL) channels are not fully reciprocal. Therefore, DL channel state information (CSI) estimated by each user equipment (UE) must be fed back to the base station (BS). However, because the channel varies between CSI acquisition and utilization, the feedback CSI may become outdated before it is used at the BS. To address this challenge, this paper proposes an UL-assisted parametric CSI feedback and prediction scheme for multi-user FDD systems with time-varying channel parameters. By exploiting the partial reciprocity between the UL and DL channel parameters, the BS first estimates the UL channel parameters from the sounding reference signals (SRSs) transmitted by the UEs. The BS then broadcasts DL pilots, allowing each UE to obtain observations containing information about its current DL channel. Instead of explicitly estimating the DL channel from these observations, each UE directly encodes them into feedback symbols and transmits the symbols to the BS. The BS decoder combines the feedback symbols with the partially reciprocal UL parameters to predict the future DL channel parameters. Finally, the corresponding DL channel matrix is synthesized from the predicted parameters using an explicit physical channel model. Simulation results on Sionna ray tracing (RT) dataset show that the proposed scheme outperforms the considered baselines in terms of channel prediction performance over different signal-to-noise ratios and prediction lengths.

title: Low-Latency LDPC Decoding Based on Consensus and Return Residual Belief Propagation
summary: We propose two new decoding algorithms for low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. The Consensus and Return residual belief propagation (C&R-RBP) algorithm reduces the number of iterations required to achieve a target decoding error rate over an AWGN channel by exploiting the availability of updated information, thereby mitigating the performance degradation caused by the greedy behavior of RBP-based algorithms and reducing error propagation. The Consensus and Delayed Return RBP algorithm (C&DR-RBP) achieves better performance in the early decoding iterations than C&R-RBP, making it particularly suitable for low-latency applications. Both proposed methods maintain the same computational complexity as the original RBP algorithm in terms of residual calculations. We also provide a formal analysis showing that the Consensus mechanism increases the probability of correct bit decisions under initial decoding conditions and in the presence of severe bit transmission errors, providing insight into the performance gains observed in the simulations. Numerical results based on the rapidly growing 5G New Radio (NR) standard, considering different code lengths, code rates, and channel models, demonstrate that both methods outperform competing RBP-based algorithms with similar overall computational complexity in terms of frame error rate (FER) and bit error rate (BER).

title: Shifted-Chart Composition for Horizon-Optimal Time-Varying LQR
comment: 7 pages, 2 figures. Submitted to the 2027 American Control Conference (ACC); under review
summary: Horizon optimization in finite-horizon LQR treats the horizon $T$ as a decision variable and adds a penalty $wT$ to the cost. Recent composition-based methods evaluate all candidate horizons in $O(Nn^3)$, instead of the $O(N^2n^3)$ of one Riccati recursion per horizon, but they track the inverse cost-to-go $P^{-1}$ and therefore require every stage and terminal cost to be positive definite, whereas LQR requires only positive semidefiniteness. This excludes costs that leave some states unpenalized. In this work, we track instead the shifted inverse $\widehat{P}_k=(P_k+cI)^{-1}$, the inverse coordinate after a symplectic shear of the state-costate variables. Its domain contains every positive semidefinite Riccati matrix, and $P_k=\widehat{P}_k^{-1}-cI$ recovers the Riccati solution. We show that the shift can be absorbed into the stage coefficients of the inverse-coordinate composition, so the $O(Nn^3)$ search carries over, exact in exact arithmetic, subject to invertibility conditions. These hold for all small $c$ when the dynamics contract the unpenalized directions, fail for at most finitely many $c$ outside a degenerate case, and are certified per horizon at run time. In our experiments, diagonal loading $Q_k+\varepsilon I$ either left cost errors several orders of magnitude above those of the shifted chart or, for small fixed $\varepsilon$, selected the wrong horizon. The shifted chart with a fixed default $c$ selected the correct horizon on all tested instances, reporting long horizons as uncertified in one stress case.

title: Memory-Coupled Unlearning for Data-Absent Identity Forgetting
summary:
Machine unlearning aims to reduce the influence of designated training data from a trained model while preserving its utility on retained data. Identity-level unlearning is particularly challenging when only limited target-specific information is available when a forgetting request is processed.
  In this work, we propose Memory-Coupled Unlearning (MCU), a framework that augments a host model with a Modern Hopfield Network (MHN) serving as a controllable external identity-prototype memory. During prototype construction, feature representations associated with each training identity are aggregated into identity prototypes and stored in the MHN. A Prototype Adaptation Network (PAN) transforms the retrieved memory representation, while a Dependency Gating Unit (DGU) controls its contribution to downstream prediction.
  When an identity is requested to be forgotten, MCU first removes the corresponding prototype from the external memory and subsequently readapts the model using limited support information associated with the target identities together with retained data. Importantly, in this work, ``data-absent'' specifically refers to the absence of the complete original forget set during request-time gradient-based readaptation; retained data may still be used to preserve downstream-task utility.
  Experiments based on the identity-partitioning and one-shot support construction of 1-SHUI show that MCU achieves a favorable empirical trade-off among model utility, membership distinguishability, and request-time computational efficiency compared with the evaluated baselines. These results provide empirical evidence for the potential of controllable external memory in machine unlearning, rather than a formal guarantee of complete information removal.

title: Enhanced Trading Systems with Intelligent Market Analysis
comment: 9 pages, 1 figure, 2 algorithms, 1 table. Accepted at ICAIA 2026 (proceedings pending)
summary: This paper proposes a hybrid reinforcement learning trading framework integrating intraday market data with transformer-based financial sentiment signals. The system extracts sentiment dynamics and semantic event clusters from financial news and incorporates them into a PPO-based trading agent. Experiments on intraday NSE data demonstrate improved risk-adjusted returns compared to price-only baselines.

title: Conflict-Aware Autonomous Resource Orchestration for 5G Edge Slicing Using Multi-Agent Systems and LLMs
comment: Accepted author manuscript for publication in the Proceedings of the 2027 IEEE Consumer Communications & Networking Conference (CCNC 2027), Las Vegas, Nevada, USA, January 9-12, 2027
summary: 5G edge network slicing must reconcile two coupled requirements: understanding high-level operator intent and reallocating scarce computing and bandwidth resources under dynamic contention. Centralized optimization can face computational and responsiveness challenges under rapidly changing edge contention, and Multi-Agent System (MAS)-based auctions can support resource arbitration but still depend on operator-defined economic parameters and priorities. Embedding a Large Language Model (LLM) directly in a recurring control loop, by contrast, may introduce non-negligible inference latency and non-deterministic behavior. This paper proposes a two-timescale architecture that addresses this gap: an LLM-based Strategist translates natural-language network intents into economic policy parameters (budget, income, and bidding-aggressiveness) at the macro scale, while a deterministic, Vickrey-inspired second-price mechanism run by SPADE-based slice agents resolves recurring resource contention at the operational scale, with the resulting allocations enforced by patching Kubernetes CPU limits and Calico CNI bandwidth annotations directly on User Plane Function pods. We evaluate the architecture end-to-end on a real Kubernetes/Open5GS edge cluster across two complementary scenarios, each repeated 30 times: a Smart-City scenario, in which natural-language public-safety intents propagate into measurable changes in slice bids and bandwidth allocations within a few auction rounds, and a Hierarchical-slicing scenario, in which the mechanism provides priority-dependent resource and QoE differentiation, adapts to abrupt demand changes, and preserves configured minimum guarantees while maintaining near-complete allocation of the shared bandwidth pool.

title: A QoE-Driven Framework for O-RAN Network Slicing Based on Empirical Multi-User VR Traffic Modelling
summary: Virtual Reality (VR) requires strict Quality-of-Experience (QoE) guarantees, making radio resource management harder. Static slice allocations are wasteful, while dynamic approaches often rely on heuristic penalty functions lacking an empirical basis. We introduce a QoE-driven network-slicing framework for Open RAN in which resource allocation is guided by empirically derived multi-user VR traffic statistics. Closed-form n-fold convolutions model the aggregate data rate and inter-arrival time of n concurrent users, validated empirically for up to four. The fitted data-rate cumulative distribution function is checked against the measured throughput to give a percentile-based satisfaction indicator; the inter-arrival law sets the slice targets. A near-real-time RIC xApp closes a loop over the E2SM-KPM and E2SM-RC interfaces to apply slice-level Physical Resource Block (PRB) quotas. On an over-the-air testbed it reclaims up to 41% of the cell's committed PRBs from a greedy neighbouring slice while never reducing the protected VR slice. An analytical study then estimates the PRB demand and per-user QoE across user counts and channel qualities, giving the admission boundary beyond which the target QoE is unattainable. A controlled comparison further shows that a fixed-rate synthetic load overstates the VR slice's PRB footprint by 68%, showing the necessity of data-driven slice dimensioning.

title: DS and AMDS Symbol-Pair Codes from Three Families of Simple Root Cyclic Codes
summary: Symbol-pair distances of simple-root cyclic codes are important for evaluating error correction performance under overlapping pair read channels. In this paper, we construct three families of simple-root cyclic codes over finite fields of odd characteristic via generator polynomials. For length \(2q+2\), the minimum symbol-pair distance is \(10\) for every odd prime power \(q\ge 7\), established by excluding invalid support configurations. For length \(4q-4\), when \(q\equiv 3\pmod 4\) and finite field constraints hold, it is \(9\) or \(10\). For length \(2(q-1)\), reciprocal-polynomial analysis shows it is \(11\) or \(12\). All obtained codes are MDS or AMDS symbol-pair codes.

title: Defending Consensus-Based Cooperative Sensing Against Conformity-Driven Byzantine Attacks in 6G UAV Swarm Networks
summary: In integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enabled six-generation (6G) networks, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms increasingly rely on consensus-based cooperative sensing: each node iteratively exchanges and fuses decisions with its neighbors to approach a global picture of the environment, supporting the high-reliability, low-latency inference demanded by mission-critical tasks. Yet this very mechanism of conformity becomes the lever of Byzantine attacks. By exploiting the update rule, malicious nodes manufacture a false consensus that lures honest nodes into drifting away from their true observations round after round, so that a normal node's actual error probability evolves dynamically and rises far above its intrinsic sensing error. Conventional fusion models, which assume node errors are fixed and independent, are therefore severely mismatched. This article argues for a different defensive perspective: instead of hunting for bad nodes, we seek to understand how good nodes turn bad, characterizing the inducement dynamics with evolutionary game theory and handing this law to the fusion center so that it can dynamically correct the true error level of normal nodes. Simulations show that the approach sustains near-perfect situational inference across a wide range of attack intensities and network sizes, while naturally supporting low latency decisions. We further discuss several open challenges on the path toward secure ISAC-6G swarm sensing.

title: Embedding Asymmetry as Attack Signal: Detecting and Defending Active Label Inference in Vertical Federated Learning
summary: Vertical federated learning lets organizations train a shared model over features they hold separately, while one party keeps the labels private. The active label inference attack of Fu et al. [12] breaks this: a feature-holding party runs a modified optimizer, MaliciousSGD, that forces class structure into its embeddings and then recovers the labels with semi-supervised learning. Defenses that perturb the shared gradient fail, because the attack acts on the party's internal optimizer, not on the message it sends. We show the attack leaves a signal the server can read from the embeddings it already receives. The adversary's Fisher class-separability pulls away from the honest party's, and the gap is visible within a few epochs. A defense triggered by this signal acts on the adversary alone. Scaling its gradient down handles few-class tasks, and a norm non-expansive projection handles many-class tasks, with the Discriminative Coverage Ratio explaining why the projection rank must grow with the class count. The defense breaks the alignment between embedding clusters and labels rather than destroying the embedding. Across four seeds on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and CINIC-10, label inference falls below what honest training already leaks, at under two points of task-accuracy cost.

title: SemTree: Judge-Aware Semantic Decision Trees for Inspectable and Repairable Rule Decisions
summary: Rule decisions such as content moderation, advertising compliance, and eligibility checks combine several conditions, exemptions, and missing-information cases, and an error can be fixed only once the failing condition is known. We introduce SemTree, a framework that represents a rule decision as a semantic decision tree: each node is a natural-language question with explicit Yes/No/Unknown criteria, a pluggable semantic judge answers it, and the branching structure is compiled on the answers that this judge actually gives. The executed path is the reasoning behind every decision, so errors are repaired where they occur: a reviewer corrects a single node and replays the rule, corrected nodes become training labels for the judge, and a tool-using LLM editor revises questions and subtrees while observing execution results. On all 8,276 ShARC test cases, a tree executed by a hosted judge reaches 67.70% accuracy with 2.99 questions per case, on par with asking the same judge for the final label (68.23%); an earlier tree compiled for a different judge scores 47.87% when executed by this judge, while a new tree compiled on this judge's answers to a 12-question initial pool already scores 64.39%. Node-level repair raises BANKING77 accuracy from 82.04% to 86.16%, an explicit exemption node cuts the false positives of a Chinese e-commerce moderation clause from 24 to 5, and a trained editor raises the development accuracy of edited trees from 64.47% to 73.35%.

title: Clock-Free Stochastic Scheduling for Real-Time Synchronized Content Delivery
comment: 15 pages, 12 figures. Full technical report containing complete proofs and appendices
summary: Real-time synchronized content delivery is critical for applications such as cloud gaming, collaborative mixed reality, and live streaming, where a server must ensure that a group of users perceives the same content simultaneously for each delivery. Due to heterogeneous and unpredictable network delays, ensuring synchronization is highly challenging. We propose a clock-free scheduling framework that introduces latency compensation to control the server's delivery time for each user, aiming to maximize synchronization performance (i.e., minimizing the gap between the maximum and minimum latencies) while maintaining a low overall latency cost. Unlike prior work requiring synchronized clocks or client-side timestamps, our approach uses only acknowledgment feedback, enabling flexible deployment across diverse environments. We formulate the problem as a convex stochastic optimization with a non-smooth objective. To solve the problem, we employ the stochastic proximal point (SPP) algorithm that updates the delay compensation, using only the previous latency samples, rather than the latency distribution. By exploiting the subproblem structure, we apply ADMM to enable efficient updates with per-iteration complexity of at most $\mathcal{O}(N\log N)$, where $N$ is the number of users. We establish a convergence rate of $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{K})$, where $K$ is the number of content deliveries for transmission. The framework is further extended to handle transmission failures, where packet loss results in successful delivery to only a subset of users. Finally, simulations using both synthetic and real-world latency traces demonstrate the consistent superiority of our algorithm against baseline methods.

title: Point-Supervised Visual Learning for GNSS Measurement Quality Assessment
summary: Multipath and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) propagation degrade global navigation satellite system (GNSS) positioning accuracy in urban environments. Although fisheye sky segmentation identifies obstructions along satellite directions, binary visibility does not fully characterize observation quality. This study proposes a point-supervised visual framework that predicts GNSS observation faults from fisheye images using supervision derived from GNSS observations. During offline labeling, a vision-assisted differential GNSS procedure selects multiple reference satellites based on sky visibility and elevation constraints. Double-difference pseudorange residuals automatically generate fault labels and sample importance weights at satellite projection locations. A residual-weighted loss is computed only at valid labeled points, enabling learning from sparse supervision without manual pixelwise fault annotations. The trained network generates dense fault probability maps, which are sampled at satellite projection locations to weight observations in weighted least squares positioning, reducing the influence of potentially faulty observations. The framework is evaluated using U-Net, DeepLabv3+, DINOv3, and SAM3 on urban vehicle data collected on a different day from the training data. All four models reduce horizontal root mean square error (RMSE) by 29.51% to 36.07% compared with SAM binary sky segmentation, with U-Net achieving the lowest RMSE of 0.78 m. The framework also provides positioning solutions during some intervals when the segmentation baseline fails. These results demonstrate the framework's generalization ability and show that GNSS-derived point supervision enables fisheye images to provide observation quality information beyond binary sky visibility, supporting GNSS fault detection.

title: DeepTelecom: A Differentiable Multimodal Framework for Channel Twinning in Dynamic Heterogeneous Wireless Environments
summary: Large-scale multimodal data are a key enabler for integrating large generative artificial intelligence models into wireless networks. However, existing wireless datasets offer limited support for heterogeneous environments, particularly in terms of reusable high-fidelity scenes, scalable differentiable ray tracing, and synchronized multimodal data. These limitations are more pronounced in mobile and aerial scenarios with time-varying environments and channels. To address these limitations, we propose DeepTelecom, a material-aware, high-fidelity multimodal channel dataset and reproducible generation framework for networks involving unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces. DeepTelecom refines coarse indoor/outdoor reconstructions and uses a large language model to map segmented surfaces to frequency-dependent electromagnetic parameters, yielding material-aware Level of Detail 3 digital twins. Then, a differentiable GPU-accelerated Sionna ray tracer simulates propagation across the sub-6 GHz/millimeter-wave/sub-terahertz bands, and specifically captures rotor-induced micro-Doppler signatures of stationary or moving UAVs at different pitch angles and translational velocities. The framework synchronously produces channel tensors, coverage maps, transmission videos, multi-view images, and weather-conditioned renderings, and supports differentiable material calibration from sparse channel anchors. The released dataset contains 10 material-aware indoor/outdoor scenes and 50,000 synchronized UAV samples; the framework supports scalable generation of additional data for user-defined scenes and system configurations. In 3D UAV localization, DeepTelecom reduces the 90th-percentile error from 31.05 m to 2.43 m compared with schemes considering only channel state information, demonstrating its significance for artificial-intelligence-enabled wireless systems.

title: Decision-Focused Learning for Optimal Battery Scheduling Under Load and Photovoltaic Power Uncertainty in Microgrids
comment: 20 pages, 13 figures, submitted to Sustainable Energy, Grids and Networks
summary: The increasing penetration of renewable energy sources in microgrids demands accurate day-ahead forecasting to support optimal battery energy storage system (BESS) scheduling. Yet the conventional predict-then-optimize paradigm trains forecasters on statistical accuracy metrics that are agnostic to the asymmetric and time-varying cost impacts of forecast errors. This work proposes a decision-focused learning (DFL) framework that trains gated recurrent unit forecasters for both load demand and photovoltaic generation directly on the downstream operational cost of a two-stage energy management system, where day-ahead BESS commitments are fixed prior to real-time balancing. Gradients are backpropagated from the real-time operational cost through both optimization stages to the forecaster weights via implicit differentiation, enabling the forecasters to internalize the penalty structure of the scheduling problem. The framework is validated on the MG2Lab experimental microgrid testbed at Politecnico di Milano across two operational scenarios of increasing grid constraint and eight forecasting configurations comprising single-source and combined-forecaster settings. Results illustrate that the DFL-trained pipeline reduces operational cost by 3.78% under normal grid conditions and by 30.60% under grid-constrained conditions relative to the accuracy- optimized baseline, while nearly eliminating load shedding events. Notably, the DFL forecasters exhibit higher statistical errors than their accuracy-trained counterparts yet achieve consistently lower operational costs, confirming that forecast accuracy and decision quality do not share a monotonic relationship in constrained microgrid scheduling.

title: Physical Side-Channel Attacks on Edge LLMs: Extracting Output Tokens and User Prompts
summary: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) on edge devices is largely motivated by privacy concerns over sharing sensitive user data with cloud servers. In this paper, we demonstrate that keeping inference local does not eliminate privacy risks: an adversary with physical access to the device may exploit hardware leakage to recover sensitive information without compromising or modifying the software system. In particular, we present an electromagnetic (EM) side-channel attack targeting LLM inference on edge devices. Targeting LLaMA-3.2-1B-Instruct running on a Raspberry Pi 5, we demonstrate that EM traces collected during inference can leak both generated tokens and user prompts. We propose three attacks under different threat assumptions. First, a profiling attack that identifies generated tokens among 50 medical and privacy-related keywords with 97.2% accuracy on profiled words. Second, a reconstruction attack recovers the model's hidden representations and uses them to predict tokens from the full 128k-token vocabulary, achieving 94.3% accuracy on profiled classes. For unseen words, the correct token is ranked within the first 100 positions of the 128k-token vocabulary in 67% of cases, with a median rank of 54. Finally, we present a hidden-state inversion attack that uses the recovered hidden state to reconstruct user prompts semantically. Our proposed attacks require only passive EM side-channel measurements and a limited number of traces during model training. These results demonstrate that local execution alone may not guarantee the confidentiality of generated tokens and user inputs.

title: VH-GPO: Verified Handoff for LLM Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Group-relative reinforcement learning methods such as GRPO train large language model (LLM) agents by comparing rollouts for the same task. When every trajectory in a group fails with the same reward, relative advantages collapse toward zero, leaving no useful learning signal. A frozen teacher can recover from a student-visited state, but letting it complete the task makes the recovered suffix entirely teacher-generated. We ask: after repairing a student failure, when should control return to the student? We propose outcome-verified teacher-student handoff, instantiated in Verified Handoff for Group Policy Optimization (VH-GPO). The teacher provides enough support to reach a state from which the student can succeed, then returns control so that successful experience is again student-generated. Given an environment-verified teacher recovery, VH-GPO selects the earliest independently confirmed handoff point found within a bounded search budget. With Qwen2.5-1.5B, VH-GPO increases success rates over GRPO from 59.38% to 94.79% on ALFWorld and from 71.62% to 77.34% on WebShop. Improvements also hold with the 7B student, for which additional teacher and student output tokens amount to 1.77% and 2.61% of regular student rollout output tokens on ALFWorld and WebShop, respectively. Ablation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the key components. These results support using verified teacher assistance to repair failures while reinforcing the student's ability to complete tasks independently.
