We develop a receding-horizon deferred-decision trajectory optimization (DDTO) controller that combines conformal terminal-location prediction, sequential candidate rejection, capacity-constrained assignment, and candidate-contingent planning. Under exchangeability conditions for terminal and identity residuals, with predictable querying, we establish fixed-time terminal-location coverage and anytime-valid target retention. At the final replan, when one control step remains, we bound the joint probability that a tightened-set DDTO plan passes nonlinear rollout verification but capture fails. The closed-loop controller applies fallback guidance to any agent without a verified DDTO plan and, across 100 paired scenarios, captures 79% of targets under the strict control-effort budget and 85% when that budget is relaxed.

title: Fetch Me If You Can: A Comprehensive Analysis of Fetch Metadata
summary: Effective server-side defenses against cross-site attacks depend on understanding the context in which browser requests are generated. However, servers often lack the information needed to distinguish legitimate requests from potentially malicious cross-site interactions. Fetch Metadata, a security mechanism introduced in 2019, addresses this limitation by adding a set of HTTP headers to outgoing browser requests. These headers provide servers with information about a request's context and provenance, enabling them to enforce request isolation policies accordingly. However, the extent of Fetch Metadata's real-world adoption and its interaction with existing security mechanisms remain largely unexplored. In this paper, we present the first large-scale measurement study of Fetch Metadata adoption. We analyze the top 1M websites in the Tranco list to detect deployments of Fetch Metadata isolation policies and identify custom policies used in the wild. We then examine how these policies address cross-site threats and assess their security coverage. Finally, we provide the first systematic comparison of Fetch Metadata with existing client-side security mechanisms, revealing security gaps that arise from differences between client-side and server-side enforcement.

title: Agreement versus Softmax under Spatial Disambiguation
comment: 7 pages, 2 figures. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Embodied Spatial Reasoning (non-archival)
summary: ScanRefer Multiple queries require spatial disambiguation: several instances of the target class are present, and the referencer must pick one. When per-query logits were never logged, a common substitute is cross-epoch agreement. On the full ScanRefer validation set (9,508 queries; GeoClassifier with ground-truth proposals), object-level softmax is similarly miscalibrated on Unique and Multiple (ECE 0.068 vs. 0.102; the scene-bootstrap gap interval includes zero). Fixed-final agreement on the same checkpoints reports ECE 0.041 vs. 0.272 (gap +0.231). Modal-vote agreement is 0.045 vs. 0.318. Most Multiple errors are same-class wrong-instance (45.6%); geometric miss (H2) is 59.6%, and wrong-category (H1) is 16.7%. A non-monotone H1 pattern does not appear under the default fixed-final protocol, and we retract it. Logit-free thresholds rank spatially hard queries poorly. If only agreement was logged, calibrate abstention on Multiple and report wrong-instance rates with H1.

title: 2D Block OMP for Near-Field Channel Estimation with Extremely Large-Scale UPA
summary: Channel estimation for extremely large-scale uniform planar arrays (UPAs) requires exploiting near-field channel structure to reduce pilot overhead. With a specifically devised channel representation matrix, the near-field channel exhibits a 2D sparse structure, which a conventional 1D block partition might divide into multiple groups. This work develops a 2D block orthogonal matching pursuit (2D-BOMP) estimator that exploits this structure through rectangular coefficient grouping. We establish sufficient recovery conditions for noiseless and noisy measurements and compare the sufficient pilot-length requirements of 1D and 2D partitions. Numerical simulations demonstrate the estimation benefits of 2D-BOMP in estimating the near-field channels of large-scale UPAs, compared with the conventional 1D-BOMP as well as the polar-domain based OMP method.

title: Double circulant LCD codes over $\mathbb{F}_2+u\mathbb{F}_2$ and constructions for binary LCD codes
summary: Linear complementary dual (LCD) codes are linear codes that intersect their dual trivially. We study double circulant (Euclidean) LCD codes over the finite chain ring $R=\mathbb F_2+u\mathbb F_2$, where $u^2=0$. Using the Chinese Remainder Theorem and the factorization of $x^n-1$, we derive an explicit enumeration formula, with a separate treatment of the constituent corresponding to $x-1$, which is not obtained by a formal specialization of the previously known counting formula over $\mathbb F_q[u]/(u^k)$. Assuming Artin's primitive root conjecture for $2$, we show that the binary Gray images contain an asymptotically good family of rate $1/2$ whose relative distance can approach $H_2^{-1}(1/4)$ from below. More importantly from the constructive viewpoint, by combining Gray images with a known extension construction, we obtain a binary LCD code with parameters $[29,15,7]$ and construct two explicit permutation-inequivalent binary LCD codes with parameters $[45,23,9]$.

title: Wing Rock Modeling and Control for Flight-Critical Systems
summary: Aircraft equipped with delta wings are designed to be aerodynamically efficient in high-speed flight. However, at low-speed flight conditions with sufficiently high angle of attack, these vehicles often have lightly damped, close to unstable lateral-directional dynamics, such as the dutch roll mode. As a result, a delta wing aircraft often exhibits the so-called wing rock (WR) phenomenon, with a back and forth rocking motion, while the aircraft sideslip angle, the roll and the yaw angular rates remain small. In this paper, the WR dynamics are defined as a lightly damped dutch roll mode excited by airmass vortical external input, acting at or near the dutch roll natural frequency. The vortical signal comes from Fourier-Galerkin approximation of the Navier-Stokes equation, with no-penetration boundary conditions and the resulting airmass velocities are calculated by the Lorenz dynamical system of three coupled bilinear ordinary differential equations. In that context, the Lorenz bilinear dynamics become the disturbance-generator exosystem, acting on the lightly damped lateral-directional aircraft mode at or near its natural frequency, and thus exciting it to produce near oscillatory wing rocking motion. Using the proposed model, a flight control design trade study is conducted to mitigate and suppress the WR phenomenon.

title: Riemannian Suppression of Cross-Session Identity Leakage in Motor-Imagery EEG
summary: Electroencephalography (EEG) recorded for motor-imagery (MI) brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) carries subject-identifying structure that persists across sessions, allowing separately released sessions from the same person to be linked. Existing EEG identity protections use learned or additive perturbations and operate on representations other than the covariance geometry underlying MI pipelines. We ask whether cross-session identity leakage can be suppressed directly in this covariance representation without learning a privacy model. We introduce a Riemannian transform that equalizes two subject-conditioned geometric statistics: the Riemannian mean covariance and the tangent-space scatter around it, with two optional band-specific refinements. Ablations show that mean alignment and scatter whitening carry nearly all of the suppression, while the optional stages contribute small, dataset-dependent refinements. Across two public datasets and five attackers spanning four covariance-space representations, the worst attacker falls from 90.8% to 15.6% on BCI Competition IV-2a and from 90.8% to 9.9% on OpenBMI, at a cost of 7.0 and 2.1 points of MI decoding accuracy relative to the 8-30 Hz input, and no aggregation rule exceeds chance by more than two points at any batch size. The transform requires no learned privacy model, surrogate network, or gradient-based training, and is fitted on one session and applied unchanged to a held-out later session.

title: Embedding Graph Kernel Entropy (EGKE): Fine-grained Hallucination Detection for LLMs from Embeddings
summary: Hallucination detection is critical for ensuring the reliability of Large Language Models (LLMs) in real-world deployments. While recent works, such as Semantic Entropy (SE) and Kernel Language Entropy (KLE), identify hallucinations by measuring semantic disagreement across multiple generated responses using Natural Language Inference (NLI) models, these methods depend on separately loaded NLI classifiers to estimate pairwise semantic similarity, introducing significant computational overhead. We propose Embedding Graph Kernel Entropy (EGKE), a variant of Kernel Language Entropy (KLE) that replaces its NLI-derived semantic graph with a Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel applied to dense sentence embeddings generated by a BGE embedding model, while retaining KLE's graph Laplacian, heat kernel, and von Neumann entropy formulation unchanged. By computing similarities directly in a continuous embedding space, the proposed method provides a symmetric and computationally efficient alternative to NLI-based semantic comparison. We evaluate our approach across 30 experimental setups (covering multiple question-answer datasets and open-weight LLM families) using both AUROC and AUARC, and demonstrate that this RBF-based method achieves competitive hallucination detection performance against state-of-the-art methods.

title: Investigation of RIS Integration in Satellite Systems Guided by ITU-R VSAT Radiation Diagram
comment: This work has been accepted for publication in ITU Journal on Future and Evolving Technologies
summary: The introduction of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) technology marks a transformative era in modern communication systems, enhancing coverage and facilitating higher data transmission rates. While recent research has delved into the integration of RIS into satellite networks, a critical and practical gap persists concerning its implementation in the satellite-Very Small Aperture Terminal (VSAT) downlink, specifically amplifying contributions from the VSAT side. This paper addresses this gap by proposing a simple and engineering methodology to optimize RIS position and orientation, incorporating considerations for the antennas' radiation patterns and the system's topology to streamline optimization variables. The primary objective of this paper is to alleviate the double fading constraint in the reflect link without the need for active elements, achieved by leveraging the Fresnel zone of the RIS. The improvement power ratio depends on the frequency and the VSAT 's diameter. The results show that for a VSAT with diameter 1m the gain is up to 9dB at 2 GHz (S band) and up to 14dB at 4 GHz (C band). Additionally, the RIS channel equation is refined, encompassing the tropospheric attenuation and accounting for electromagnetic wave polarization.

title: Learning Rules, Memorizing Facts: An Information-Theoretic View of Hallucination
summary: Understanding the relationship between generalization and hallucination requires clarifying the role of memorization. We study this relationship from an information-theoretic perspective through a Selector-Density Conditional Mutual Information (CMI) framework. In the sparse random-fact limit, a uniformly bounded information budget per fact forces a nonvanishing false-positive rate at recall bounded away from zero, even when all facts are observed during training. In a rules-and-facts setting, we decompose model-data mutual information into rule learning, atomic-fact memory, and excess memorization, revealing competition between rule learning and factual memory even without excess memorization. A joint budget bound quantifies the resulting constraint on atomic hallucination under perfect atomic recall. Moreover, an additive Gaussian model shows that maintaining high recall for atomic and composite facts incurs false positives even under optimal data mixing. Finally, controlled relational experiments hint how training exposure, rule complexity, and model capacity shape these trade-offs.

title: A Deficiency-Based Approach for Unbalanced Three-Phase Distribution System Expansion Planning
comment: 12 pages, 1 figure, 3 tables. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible
summary: Distribution planners typically characterize grid needs through power flow studies and fit upgrades to those needs by hand. More principled one-shot optimization methods either do not scale or misrepresent unbalanced three-phase networks. This paper proposes an iterative planning process that alternates between two problem classes with mature off-the-shelf solvers. An optimal power flow (OPF) problem quantifies the deficiency of a candidate portfolio by optimizing the dispatch of controllable devices and measuring thermal and voltage violations on a common scale, with an optimal value of zero exactly at adequate portfolios. The OPF multipliers give a first-order approximation of the relief each investment candidate would provide. We bound the error of this approximation and show that structural properties of the deficiency guard it against overestimation. Building on this property, a heuristic cutting-plane search uses a mixed-integer linear program to propose each next portfolio from these approximations. On six unbalanced three-phase feeders from the SMART-DS dataset, the search outperforms a linearized optimization-based benchmark, and the results agree across five variants of the deficiency.

title: SkillMarker: A KGW-Based Watermarking Method for Agent Skill Ownership Verification
summary: Agent skills encode operational procedures and domain expertise as reusable knowledge assets, yet their distribution in plaintext exposes them to unauthorized copying and leakage. However, practical mechanisms for skill ownership verification and leakage tracing remain underdeveloped. Watermark embedding before distribution offers a potential solution, but structured, compact skill instructions impose stringent requirements for factual and procedural accuracy. To address these challenges, we introduce SkillMarker, a KGW-based watermarking method that jointly targets functionality preservation and strong watermark embedding. SkillMarker unifies quality-constrained rewriting with signal-oriented candidate search. The former separates essential knowledge from flexible expression to preserve instruction fidelity; the latter explores alternative expressions to obtain a stronger watermark signal under preservation constraints. We release an open-source toolkit that integrates watermark embedding, quality auditing, and detection to support the protection of agent skills. SkillMarker targets ownership verification and leakage tracing in distributed skill ecosystems, where content may be copied in whole or in part, or incorporated into other skills.

title: Learnable Low-Rank Polynomial Sketch for Effective Linear Attention
summary: Softmax attention in Transformers suffers from quadratic complexity in sequence length, making it impractical for long-context applications. Linear attention alleviates this issue by replacing the exponential kernel with alternative functions that enable linear-time computation. Among existing linear attention approaches, recent studies have shown that polynomial kernels are particularly effective, as they exhibit sparse and spiky behavior similar to softmax attention, which emphasizes large dot products while suppressing irrelevant interactions. However, the exact computation of high-degree polynomial kernels is infeasible for high-dimensional representations. As a result, prior work relies on approximate polynomial kernels. This introduces a non-negligible approximation error. In this paper, we show that, from the perspective of polynomial kernel approximation, existing linear attention methods are still suboptimal. We propose \textbf{L}earnable \textbf{Lo}w-Rank \textbf{P}olynomial \textbf{S}ketch (LLoPS), a principled and flexible framework for approximating polynomial kernels with linear attention. Our method learns a low-rank polynomial sketch that provably achieves a strictly smaller approximation error than existing approaches. Experiment results show that LLoPS achieves the highest performance across extensive benchmarks, comparing with various linear attention baselines.

title: Generative Deep Learning for CSI Feedback in Massive MIMO via Channel Distribution Prediction
summary: Existing deep-learning-based channel state information (CSI) feedback methods reduce feedback overhead by compressing high-dimensional CSI into low-dimensional representations and/or exploiting historical CSI to predict future CSI. However, these methods may become unreliable when user equipment (UE) suddenly changes its motion. To address this issue, we propose a prediction-aided coding (PAC) framework for generative CSI feedback, which adaptively encodes CSI based on predicted channel/CSI distributions and the observed CSI in real time. Each CSI frame is represented by multiple CSI tokens obtained without using historical CSI, making token generation robust to abrupt UE motion. In the first stage, the conditional distribution, instead of a deterministic value, of the next-frame CSI tokens is predicted based on historical tokens. In the second stage, once the next frame arrives, the predicted distribution is used for variable-length entropy coding of its CSI tokens. To further reduce feedback overhead and inference latency, we propose efficient designs for both stages. For the first stage, a customized causal Transformer with a new positional embedding strategy accurately predicts next-frame token probabilities. For the second stage, a parallel causal decoding strategy reduces the inference latency caused by sequential token decoding. Extensive experiments show that, compared with existing history-aware baselines, PAC reduces feedback overhead by approximately 72% to 84% while achieving higher reconstruction accuracy. Additionally, PAC maintains CSI reconstruction accuracy under random-walk trajectories, whereas existing history-aware baselines suffer sharp degradation in reconstruction accuracy.

title: RPA Decoding with Few Subspace Projections for Correcting Structured Error Patterns in RM Codes
comment: Submitted to IEEE Information Theory Workshop (ITW) 2027
summary: The Recursive Projection Aggregation (RPA) decoder for Reed-Muller codes uses, in its default implementation, all one-dimensional subspaces at each level of recursion. We restrict our attention to the case where the number of errors is $t<d_{\mathrm{min}}/2$. It is known that if the number of errors is $t<d_{\mathrm{min}}/2$, then $2t+1$ subspaces at each level of recursion are sufficient to correct these errors. We show that, for structured error patterns, the number of subspaces required for correction can be reduced further by appropriately selecting the subspaces used for projection. In particular, when errors occur as a single burst of length $t < d_{\mathrm{min}}/2$, three subspaces at each level of recursion suffice for correction. We obtain similar results for multiple bursts and other structured error patterns as well.

title: Coordinated Conservation Voltage Reduction and Network Topology Reconfiguration in Active Distribution Networks
summary: Distribution networks rely on conservation voltage reduction (CVR) and network topology reconfiguration (NTR) to manage demand, distributed energy resources (DERs), and tighter operating margins. Yet these strategies are typically deployed independently, despite coupled effects on feeder voltages, losses, and loading. This paper addresses that gap by developing a day-ahead mixed-integer second order cone programming (MISOCP) framework that jointly optimizes feeder head voltage control and network reconfiguration. The formulation incorporates AC branch flow constraints, ZIP load models, DERs, battery energy storage systems, and multi substation radiality. Using modified IEEE 33 bus and 123 bus systems, four configurations isolate the individual and coordinated effects of CVR and NTR. On the 33-bus system under mixed ZIP loading, NTR reduces active energy loss by 2.50%, while coordinated operation reduces it by 2.91% relative to SDN and produces a 2.46% CVR induced active load reduction relative to SDNTR. Under constant impedance loading, coordinated operation reduces active energy loss by 17.65% relative to SDN, while CVR reduces active load by 14.61% relative to SDNTR. DER portfolio scaling shows a nonmonotonic coordinated load reduction response, strongest at 20% penetration and decreasing at higher levels. On the 123 bus system, NTR reduces losses by 19.3%, while CVR reduces voltage dependent load energy by 2.3 to 2.4%. Under loading stress, SDN becomes infeasible at 120% loading, whereas CEDNTR remains feasible. Overall, the results demonstrate complementary, operating condition dependent benefits shaped by load composition, DER portfolio scaling, feeder topology, voltage margins, and source constraints, highlighting the value of joint optimization.

title: LLM-based Code Auditing by Inferring and Evaluating Developer Assumptions
summary:
When we see a null pointer check, we know that the developer believes that the pointer may not be initialized. If the same pointer is later used without a null pointer check, we may consider this a violation of the developer's belief and ultimately a bug. We develop such a belief-guided program analysis for vulnerability detection (VD). For example, when an authentication function returns the same error for both, a wrong user name and a wrong password, an auditor may infer that the developer believes that both cases are indistinguishable, mitigating a user enumeration attack. This belief is reasonable, as it follows standard security practice. Yet, a function call inducing a difference in response time for both cases, contradicts this belief. This contradiction uncovers a timing side-channel that syntactic analysis tools would miss. Existing static analysis tools struggle with this type of flaw because they require them to be expressible by general, syntactic patterns. Our belief-guided approach detects such domain-specific, high-level semantic security flaws that remain elusive.
  Given a function, our approach, Creed, infers the developer's security-related beliefs, evaluates how reasonable each one is, and derives the conditions under which it is violated. In contrast to existing ML-based VD techniques, Creed explains the root cause, the symptoms, and the conditions under which each issue is exploitable. To address the context-dependency problem in the evaluation, we introduce two measures for explanation-based VD: recall quantifies how effectively an approach correctly explains a known vulnerability, and overhead quantifies the effort of inspecting its reports. On a recent real-world vulnerability benchmark, Creed detects both semantic and syntactic vulnerabilities more effectively than existing explanation-based VD tools, achieving the best effectiveness-effort trade-off.

title: Learning Non-Gaussian SEMs with Conditional Risk, and Why the Direction of Recursion Matters
summary: Variance-based methods recover a Gaussian linear structural equation model (SEM) with equal or suitably constrained error variances, either by recursively identifying the source nodes with smallest conditional variance (top-down method) or sink nodes with highest conditional variance (bottom-up method). We show that the use of conditional variance is incidental: replacing it with the conditional risk, i.e., the minimal expected loss of linear prediction under the negative log-likelihood of the noise distribution, extends both methods to non-Gaussian noise. Existing methods are the least-squares special case. This yields two main results. First, exploiting the noise distribution improves structure recovery: the matched-loss procedures recover the SEM more accurately than their least-squares counterparts and the LiNGAM methods, which are designed for non-Gaussianity. Second, the two methods, interchangeable in the Gaussian setting, separate under non-Gaussian noise: the top-down method is correct for every noise density with finite differential entropy, whereas the bottom-up method requires a regularity condition and can fail without it, for instance under mean-zero exponential or Cauchy noise. Simulations confirm both results.

title: Practical Hardware-Efficient ISAC: Enabling Multi-Target Sensing With Few RF Chains
summary: Hybrid analog--digital arrays reduce hardware cost in integrated sensing and communications (ISAC), but spatial compression and beam-dependent scan responses complicate multi-target estimation with few radio-frequency (RF) chains. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a burst beam-scanning multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) framework that reuses downlink reference signals for joint range, radial-velocity, elevation, and azimuth estimation. Specifically, a structured global--local dual-tensor estimator separates targets by using scanning observations and refines their parameters from selected-beam RF-chain responses, with delay--Doppler signatures maintaining cross-stage target correspondence. The recovered subarray responses yield closed-form elevation and azimuth estimates through exact sum--difference relations, avoiding small-angle approximations and fine angular grid searches. To further improve Doppler accuracy, spatial-mask-aided weighted least squares exploits the longer inter-burst temporal aperture while resolving phase ambiguity using intra-burst estimates. The joint multi-target Cramér--Rao lower bound (CRLB) and corresponding three-dimensional (3D) positioning bound are also derived to characterize estimation performance. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme achieves near-CRLB estimation accuracy at high transmit powers and centimeter- to millimeter-level 3D positioning with only four RF chains, while maintaining low computational cost.

title: Generalized Hamming Weights and Subcode Support Weight Distributions of Twisted Reed-Solomon Codes
summary: In this paper, we determine the generalized Hamming weight hierarchies of two classes of twisted Reed--Solomon (TRS) codes. For TRS codes with one twist, we first determine all possible values of the generalized Hamming weights. We then give a complete characterization of the weight hierarchy in terms of the minimum distance of the dual code. Explicit conditions are derived for the minimum distances of the code and its dual, which make the whole weight hierarchy explicitly computable. As special cases, the obtained results recover several known characterizations for TRS codes to be MDS, NMDS codes, and $s$-gap AMDS codes. For TRS codes with two twists, we similarly determine the complete generalized Hamming weight hierarchy. In this case, the higher generalized Hamming weights are determined by the first two generalized Hamming weights of the dual code, for which explicit rank conditions are also obtained. In addition, we further determine the subcode support weight distributions of this class of single-twist TRS codes. More precisely, for each $1 \le r \le k$, we derive an explicit formula for the number of $r$-dimensional subcodes with a prescribed support size, thereby giving a complete description of the support distribution of subcodes.

title: Reduced-Order Backstepping Control of Nonlinear Mechanical Systems with Input Delay via Galerkin Projection
comment: Accepted for presentation at the 65th IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC 2026)
summary: This paper addresses trajectory tracking for a class of nonlinear mechanical systems with input delay. The delayed actuator channel is represented as an equivalent transport partial differential equation, thereby transforming the original delayed system into a coupled plant-channel representation. A finite-dimensional approximation of the delay channel is then constructed through Galerkin projection, resulting in an explicit ODE model of the delayed actuator dynamics. Using this reduced-order plant-channel model, a backstepping controller is developed, and Lyapunov analysis establishes uniform exponential stability of the nominal tracking error dynamics for the reduced-order Galerkin model. To enhance practical implementation, a command-filtered version is also introduced to avoid direct differentiation of virtual controls, for which a corresponding uniform ultimate boundedness result is obtained. Simulation studies are provided to validate the proposed design and illustrate the effectiveness of the method.

title: Privacy Conductor: An Architectural Enforcement of Contextual Integrity in LLM-Based Document Retrieval
summary: Large language model (LLM) that retrieve internal documents within an organization must decide who may receive them. Existing approaches based on Contextual Integrity ask the model to make that decision, so access depends on probabilistic reasoning. We present Privacy Conductor, an architecture that removes the decision from the model: a deterministic gate enforces a policy written by an authority, and the model receives only what the requester may already see. On a synthetic clinical corpus of 2,520 requester--document flows, the gate reproduces its policy exactly, so the remaining risk lies in the document labels it reads. As label source is of primary importance, we compare LLM and human generated labels. Across seven configurations of six models from two model families, LLM-written labels degrade the policy in every case. Models assign a document's sensitivity tier correctly on 78--86% of documents, but reproduce its access-control list on as few as 23%. Relabeling the same documents five times with an identical request changes 13 to 124 access decisions per configuration, a result that does not depend on our own labels. On 214 flows from HIPAA court cases, the most accurate configuration (87.8%) still permits 11 of the 20 disclosures the law prohibits. LLMs can describe what a document contains, but not decide who should receive it. Hence, we recommend privacy policy should be authored by accountable personnel and enforced outside the model.

title: Adaptive-Depth Is a Finishing Stage
comment: Accepted for poster presentation at the AXIOM Workshop (Foundations of Efficient Deep Learning) at NeurIPS 2026. 9 pages, 8 figures
summary: Looped transformers reuse the same layer multiple times, allowing inference compute to be adjusted without changing the model. Recent adaptive-depth methods train the model across multiple loop depths from the beginning of training. We introduce fixed-first training, which varies model depth only during a short final phase of training. At 200M parameters, training a model of fixed-depth 2 for the first 67% of the run reduces modeled training compute by 45% while keeping mean negative log-likelihood (NLL) across inference depths within 0.5% of training across depths throughout. At 1B parameters, training initially at depth 4 reduces modeled compute by 31% to 37% and wall-clock time by 32% to 39%, while keeping final NLL within 0.8% and downstream differences within the observed seed variation. These results show that training over the full range of depths can be reserved for a short finishing phase with only small changes in performance.

title: Scattering-Mediated NLOS Ultraviolet Communication: Channel Characterization, Modeling, and Data Transmission
summary: Solar-blind ultraviolet (UV) optical wireless communication (OWC) enables non-line-of-sight (NLOS) transmission through atmospheric scattering. This work presents a comprehensive experimental and simulation study of a 100 m outdoor UVC link with comparative measurements under LOS-blocked and open-field conditions. The results show that LOS-blocked scattering-mediated links exhibit substantially higher path loss and narrower bandwidth than corresponding open-field measurements, highlighting the impact of residual LOS components in practical diffused beam UVC experiments. A photon-tracing Monte Carlo (MC) framework incorporating realistic transmitter/receiver characteristics and obstacle geometry is further developed to reproduce the measured channel characteristics with high accuracy. Despite the severe path loss and pulse broadening effects, reliable 20-200 kbps transmission is experimentally demonstrated over the 100 m LOS-blocked link using on-off keying (OOK) and pulse-position modulation (PPM), representing the longest-distance and highest-data-rate experimental demonstration of an explicitly LOS-blocked scattering-mediated UVC link reported to date.

title: More Interactions Make Communications More Efficient: A Directed Information Bottleneck Approach to Task-Oriented Communication
comment: Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Networking
summary: Task-oriented communication improves communication efficiency by transmitting semantic information required for downstream tasks, but may incur redundancy with previously transmitted information. To address this issue, we propose a variational directed information bottleneck joint source-channel coding (VDIB-JSCC) framework that transmits only previously unacquired information. Specifically, we use directed information to characterize the causal flow of task-relevant incremental information and theoretically demonstrate its advantages over mutual information and conditional mutual information. Based on this metric, we formulate a directed information bottleneck (DIB) objective that balances task-relevant information preservation and redundant information compression. We further derive a variational formulation, termed VDIB, whose tractable upper bound serves as the training loss. The encoder integrates a Vision Transformer for frame-wise semantic extraction and a Mamba-based causal state-space model for capturing temporal dependencies and extracting incremental information, while the decoder uses a Mamba-based state-space model for task inference. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 video streams demonstrate that VDIB-JSCC achieves higher classification accuracy with less transmitted information than state-of-the-art semantic communication methods. These results show that leveraging historical knowledge enables task completion with less information, improving communication efficiency.

title: Safety-Aware Dimension Selection for Reduced-Order Model Predictive Control
summary: Model reduction can substantially reduce the computational burden of model predictive control (MPC) for high-dimensional systems, but a reduced dimension chosen for performance may be insufficient for safety-critical operation. This paper introduces a safety-aware dimension-selection framework in which the prediction model adapts to the order of the model required to maintain a certified finite-horizon safety condition. Dynamic active subspaces provide a performance-oriented ordering of reduced coordinates, while finite-horizon error bounds robustly enforce discrete-time control barrier function constraints. The controller selects the smallest prediction order for which the resulting safety-critical MPC problem remains feasible. We establish full-order horizon safety, recursive feasibility, and closed-loop invariance of the safe set under the proposed reduced-order formulation. The proposed approach therefore adapts the prediction complexity to safety requirements, avoiding unnecessary high-dimensional prediction during benign operation.

title: Penetrating the Reality Wall: Long-Range and Through-Wall AR/VR Privacy Eavesdropping via Wireless Power Side Channel
summary:
Over the past decade, Metaverse technology (AR/VR) has seen widespread adoption in numerous areas, including gaming, social networking, and online collaboration. Although recent studies have exposed vulnerabilities in VR systems, they often apply methods (e.g., pre-installed malicious apps or scripts) from conventional mobile platforms directly, demonstrating impractical attacks that fail to investigate unique privacy leakages specific to VR platforms. In this paper, we present an orthogonal attempt to analyze the attack surface of the power side channel on AR/VR's network connection by capturing the through-wall wireless power in the network transmission medium (e.g., Wi-Fi signals) non-intrusively in a comparatively long distance (e.g., 5.0m-8.0m) and further reconstructing multi-level privacy-aware user behaviors.
  We propose MetaSpy to validate the feasibility and practicality of our disclosed wireless power-based traffic analysis attack. It first captures through-wall wireless power transmitted from the Wi-Fi router of an adjacent room, identifies the device type, then infers (i) user interactions such as browsing websites, running AR/VR apps, and performing various in-app activities, (ii) unseen VR-specific activities in VR games (e.g., Population: ONE), and (iii) avatar-based user re-identification and virtual keystroke inference corresponding to head movements. We evaluated the effectiveness of MetaSpy in four commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) VR headsets, and the empirical results demonstrate its competitive accuracy in unveiling multi-level user privacy within virtual scenes in through-wall settings at a longer distance (1.8x-80x) than most of the recent studies, and it shows resilience to a series of external interference and impact factors. In addition, we also propose and evaluate effective countermeasures to protect data confidentiality in AR/VR wireless transmission.

title: Do Artificial Neural Networks Need Dendritic Nanotubes? Two Reasons for Shrinking Importance Estimates in Continual Learning
comment: Github: https://github.com/Saurav-K-Aryal/Do-Artificial-Neural-Networks-Need-Dendritic-Nanotubes-.git 21 pages, 3 figures, 10 tables. Simulation and figure scripts are included as ancillary files
summary: Regularization-based continual learning protects each parameter in proportion to an estimate of its importance, yet these estimates come from finite samples and heuristics and are used as if they were exact. We report four studies that start from a biologically inspired mechanism and end with a statistical explanation of it. Motivated by dendritic nanotubes, we let transient lateral links diffuse importance tags between hidden units. Links between co-active units gave no significant gain, but random links with lifetimes of 25 or 200 steps raised final accuracy on 20-task Permuted MNIST by 1.5 to 2.6 points. We show that random diffusion implements linear shrinkage of importance toward the layer mean in expectation. A simulation of the link process alone predicts shrinkage weights of 0.23 and 0.52 for these lifetimes, and graph-free shrinkage at 0.25 and 0.5 reproduces both the accuracy and the dispersion of the consolidated importance, while every activity-dependent rule did worse than random links. A five-seed screen across EWC, SI, and MAS found nominal gains for SI and MAS on Permuted MNIST and losses on task-incremental Split CIFAR-100, where forgetting was small and shrinkage cost plasticity. Varying the number of importance samples then separates two mechanisms on Permuted MNIST. For EWC, the gain fell by about ten points per tenfold increase in samples, from 19.6 points with 10 samples to -0.4 with 1000, a variance effect. For MAS, a gain of about one point persisted at 1000 samples, consistent with a bias in the importance measure rather than noise. Shrinkage had no detectable effect for MAS on a domain-incremental CIFAR-100 benchmark. Finally, we show that a standard heteroscedastic empirical Bayes rule shrinks the largest Fisher-type estimates most, which may explain its poor results, and point to a log-scale alternative.

title: Solar-Blind Ultraviolet Communication: Taxonomy and Experimental Characterization
summary: Solar-blind ultraviolet communication (UVC) exploits near-zero solar background radiation and strong atmospheric scattering in the 200-280 nm band, enabling photon-level daytime communication and propagation modes beyond conventional line-of-sight (LOS) links. However, existing studies mainly focus on individual channel types, and a unified channel classification is still lacking. This paper presents a taxonomy of all four fundamental solar-blind UVC channels together with representative experimental validations and a comparative performance analysis. The proposed framework provides practical guidelines for selecting appropriate channel architectures for future solar-blind UVC systems.

title: Log Density Spectrum Based Decoding of Polar Codes for Channels with Strong Phase Noise
summary: A decoding method is proposed for polar codes under channels with strong phase noise. In contrast to traditional SC decoding, where recursions are performed on scalar soft information such as probabilities, the proposed decoding recurses over probability density functions defined on the phase-noise variable. To make the density-level recursion computationally tractable, we represent each log-density by its spectrum, and derive approximate formulas for the spectrum recursion, therefore, the proposed method is termed log-density spectrum recursion (LDSR). Numerical results are given under strong phase noise and AWGN, showing that a prominent superiority of error performance is achieved by LDSR in comparison with traditional SC and Kalman-based methods.

title: Stabilizing Low-Stiffness Soft Robots at Unstable Equilibria: A Model-Based Optimal Control Approach
summary: Continuum soft robots are highly nonlinear and underactuated systems, which makes stabilizing them around unstable equilibrium points difficult. This challenge becomes even greater in low stiffness regimes, where gravitational forces dominate elastic forces. In this letter, we explore whether optimal control can address these challenges using a computa- tionally efficient method suitable for real time use. We propose a nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) approach based on Differential Dynamic Programming (DDP), combined with an accurate reduced order Variable Strain model with analytical derivatives. This results in an efficient control framework for addressing the stabilization problem. Tested on a soft inverted pendulum and other hybrid soft rigid systems, the method outperforms traditional controllers, stabilizes more challenging configurations, and operates reliably at real time speeds (50 150 Hz), demonstrating both effectiveness and practical feasibility in experimental settings.

title: What the Model Cannot See: Covert and Provable Text Invisibility in LLMs
summary: Text wrapped in a trigger can be made behaviorally invisible to a language model: omitted from summaries and quotations, ignored in question answering, and left unflagged by downstream filtering. We study this selective blindness as a dual-use information-flow primitive, a supply-chain backdoor, and a white-box auditing problem. We first implement it exactly as a serving-time span veto: blocking information flow out of a marked span makes every outside activation bit-identical under same-length substitution of the span's content, a noninterference property we verify across ten models, seven mixer families, and 0.5B-120B parameters. The veto serves as a deployable quarantine, an exact reference for calibrating leakage, and a teacher. Distilled into weights, it yields a backdoor: checkpoints trained on six model families from 4B to 120B ignore marked context at little benchmark cost, and their outputs show no measurable semantic trace of the suppressed content above the veto reference on our held-out suite; an in-domain variant suppresses planted vulnerabilities during AI code review. Detection is therefore a white-box problem. Simpler backdoors remain internally transparent -- linear probes recover suppressed content at 0.57-0.79 accuracy versus 0.025 chance -- but hardening the attack until probes reach chance collapses attention from outside the span into it below the range of base models. Across the attacks we evaluate, probe visibility trades off against routing visibility; we do not establish that this tradeoff is fundamental.

title: Variance Fingerprints: Component-Wise Identification of Content Factors by Augmentation Design
summary: Augmentation-based self-supervised learning can recover the content shared across views without separating its underlying factors into individual coordinates. We ask whether augmentations can be designed to make those factors identifiable. Our approach allows content factors to fluctuate across augmented views while preserving their mean for each source instance. Each instance receives a fixed, recorded set of augmentation strengths that controls how much its factors fluctuate. When factors respond differently to changes in these strengths, their patterns of variation provide information that distinguishes them. Under suitable decoder and support assumptions, we prove that these differences identify individual factors in a conditional Gaussian model, up to permutation, scaling, and translation. We then develop a learner that uses the recorded strengths to estimate these patterns jointly across instances, enabling learning from few views per instance. Synthetic experiments demonstrate near-perfect factor recovery through nonlinear mixing. Controlled dSprites experiments show improved coordinate alignment using augmentations that target known factors, even without telling the learner which augmentation corresponds to which representation coordinate. These results suggest a route to component identification in self-supervised learning: augmentation design can supply identifying information beyond shared content alone.

title: On the CSIT-Limited Delay Robustness of IR-HARQ in Finite Blocklength RSMA Networks
summary: This letter studies the throughput and reliability of power-constrained rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) with variable-length incremental-redundancy hybrid automatic repeat request (IR-HARQ) under finite blocklength (FBL) transmission and imperfect channel state information at the transmitter (CSIT). While perfect-CSIT feedback-delay tolerance approaches a natural ceiling as signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) grows, we show imperfect CSIT imposes a strictly lower, finite ceiling set solely by CSIT quality, one that transmit power cannot overcome. We derive analytical expressions and tight approximations for common- and private-stream decoding failure probabilities, capturing FBL and CSIT uncertainty via a unified CSIT-degradation factor. Also, we show that residual interference saturates effective stream power at high SNR, limiting reliability and producing this delay-tolerance ceiling. Simulations validate the analysis and quantify the ceiling, offering design insights for delay-robust RSMA under imperfect CSIT.

title: Multiple-Function Approximated Coded Computing: Constructions and Error Bounds
summary: Coded computing mitigates stragglers in distributed computation. While Lagrange coded computing (LCC) enables exact polynomial computation over finite fields, Berrut approximated coded computing (BACC) enables approximate computation of arbitrary, including non-polynomial, functions in the analog domain. In applications such as multi-task learning and inference, multiple functions must be evaluated over different subsets of a common dataset, making single-round computation desirable to reduce communication overhead. An existing LCC approach addresses this requirement but is restricted to polynomial functions over finite fields, leaving single-round multi-function computation in the analog domain an open problem. In this work, we develop a single-round construction for computing multiple arbitrary functions using BACC. We first extend the existing multi-function computation approach in LCC to the BACC setting and derive an approximation-error bound. Building on this, we propose a construction based on Berrut basis functions for computing multiple arbitrary functions and derive its approximation-error bound. We analyze the scaling of both bounds with the number of functions and the number of data points per function, and numerically compare the two constructions over a wide range of arbitrary functions. The results demonstrate that the proposed construction achieves lower relative errors than the existing approach in the tested settings.

title: Reach-Avoid Certificates for Contact-based Stochastic Hybrid Systems
summary: This work studies certified reach-avoid control of stochastic hybrid systems in which a stochastic differential equation governs continuous flow and a controlled stochastic kernel governs guard-triggered resets. The input appears only in the reset kernel, where it determines the post-jump distribution. Certificates for such systems have so far assumed spontaneous or controller-chosen jump times, a finite horizon, or discrete-time dynamics; we certify, over the infinite horizon, that the target is reached before the unsafe set with at least a prescribed probability. First, we introduce reach-avoid contact certificates, whose flow and jump conditions are imposed only on a sublevel corridor, and prove that any such certificate with a compatible reset policy meets the specification; a pointwise safety filter extends this guarantee from verification to control by constraining arbitrary nominal controllers. Next, we prove that executions are non-Zeno and bound the expected settling time and reset count. We frame certificate search as a linear program over any twice-differentiable dictionary followed by independent verification. We illustrate our approach via comparisons where the certified region is a subset covering 93.6\% of the ground truth and where our certificate-based safety filter reaches the goal while reducing collisions from 68 to zero across 200 episodes of a dribbling ball problem.

title: Forensic Text Recovery from Document Thumbnails Using Text-Aware U-Net
comment: 6 pages. Published in the proceedings of ICAIBD 2026
summary: Forensic analysis of low-resolution Word thumbnails presents a significant challenge because these artifacts may constitute the only remaining visual evidence of deleted documents. Standard Optical Character Recognition (OCR) tools perform poorly on such severely degraded images, creating a critical bottleneck in forensic evidence recovery. Although deep learning architectures, such as U-Net, can improve visual image quality, models optimized solely using pixel-based loss functions tend to favor visual smoothness over the structural fidelity required for accurate text recognition. To address this limitation, we propose a text-aware restoration framework designed for forensic triage. The proposed approach employs a U-Net architecture guided by a hybrid optimization strategy that integrates pixel-level fidelity with machine-readable text constraints. Specifically, an OCR-based Normalized Levenshtein Distance (NLD) metric is used during model selection to prioritize the recovery of an accurate character topology. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly reduces the NLD, enabling reliable recovery of machine-readable text from severely degraded thumbnails.

title: The RNN Homunculus: Learning to Gate Long-Term Memory
summary: Learning long-range dependencies with recurrent neural networks (RNNs) is difficult because of the vanishing gradient problem. Gated recurrent neural networks like GRUs and LSTMs address this problem and are commonly explained by their ability to create additive copy paths through time. This explanation is correct, but incomplete: useful RNN gate values must themselves be learned, which is typically done with another RNN. We study this gate-learning problem through carefully controlled sequence classification tasks. Our analysis shows that gated architectures struggle when all training samples require long-range memory and thus equally suffer from the vanishing gradient problem. We intervene by adding short-dependency samples which let gated models learn solutions that capture long-dependency samples, but also generalize across different class labels. When properly learned, gated RNNs match or even exceed the test accuracy of modern architectures like Mamba and xLSTM. Overall, our results highlight gate learning as a central part of learning long-range memory and show how training data can support this process by exposing the same task over shorter dependencies.

title: Colored Graph Signal Diffusion Models
summary: Standard diffusion processes with isotropic noise corruption are not spectrally neutral. They inherit a coarse-to-fine generation hierarchy from the nonuniform data spectrum, because each frequency band loses signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) at its own rate. For signals on a graph, the relevant spectrum is that of the graph shift operator (GSO). A natural construction, therefore, builds both the diffusion dynamics and the denoiser from graph filters of the GSO, and any such design also takes a position on this hierarchy. We expose this hierarchy as a tunable axis through a family of colored score-based diffusions. Fixing the terminal prior to a Gaussian colored by the GSO couples the drift and diffusion through a positive spectral rate, which acts as a clock for each graph-frequency band. The clock sets when a band loses and recovers information, and the forward processes of standard and certain graph-aware diffusions appear as members of this family. A GSO-valued EDM preconditioning splits the denoiser into an analytic Wiener head that carries the Gaussian second-order structure and a graph neural network (GNN) that learns the remaining non-Gaussian dependencies. Numerical experiments show that colored diffusions reach a given generation quality in far fewer sampling steps than standard diffusion.

title: Covering Radius and Deep Holes of Hyperderivative Reed-Solomon Codes under the NRT Metric
summary: The deep hole problem is a fundamental problem in coding theory, and it has many important applications in code constructions and cryptography. The deep hole problem of Reed-Solomon codes has gained a lot of attention. As a generalization of Reed-Solomon codes under Hamming metric, we study the covering radius and deep holes of Hyperderivative Reed-Solomon (HRS) codes under the Niederreiter-Rosenbloom-Tsfasman (NRT) metric. We determine the NRT covering radius of HRS code and characterize its NRT deep holes via Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) extensions and polynomial remainder conditions. We further relate the enumeration of NRT deep holes to the characteristic polynomial of an associated hyperplane arrangement. We also provide three classes of explicit NRT deep-hole constructions, propose a Cheng-Murray type conjecture for HRS codes under the NRT metric and obtain a conditional low-layer description. Using these characterizations, we derive exact enumeration formulas in several special cases.

title: STATCOM-Based Flicker Mitigation in Electric Arc Furnace Systems Using DQ-PI and Lyapunov-Based Nonlinear Control
comment: 18 pages, plus a 7-page supplementary document. Compiled with pdfLaTeX
summary: Electric arc furnaces inject stochastic reactive-power swings that cause voltage flicker at the point of common coupling. This paper compares two STATCOM inner controllers for an 11~kV, 50~Hz furnace feeder: a split-frequency DQ-PI design and a Lyapunov-based nonlinear design whose integral state is retained in the storage function, giving global asymptotic stability of the nominal unsaturated current-error subsystem. Gains for both controllers were tuned by a frozen metaheuristic campaign and then evaluated over 600~s with an IEC~61000-4-15 digital flickermeter. A post-campaign audit showed that the stochastic arc realization used for the original comparison was periodic, so the two selected gain sets were frozen without retuning or reselection and evaluated on ten independent stochastic realizations that had been specified and archived before the STO-ENS validation campaign, together with a paired uncompensated case for each realization. Both controllers reduce the mean short-term flicker severity by about 62% relative to the STO-ENS uncompensated baseline, and no statistically detectable difference in mean flicker severity is found between them. They separate instead in realization sensitivity: the Lyapunov standard deviation across arcs is roughly one third that of DQ-PI. Controller ordering inferred from a single stochastic trajectory is therefore not a reliable measure of stochastic robustness, and ensemble validation is necessary.

title: Scalable Weak-to-Strong Verifier Hardening for Agent Environments
summary:
Agent environments are essential for large language model (LLM) development. They use programmatic verifiers to turn complex outcomes into rewards. Verifiers can be attacked into awarding full credit to cheating agents without completing the intended task, causing inaccurate evaluation and misalignment in training. As agent environments scale in numbers and difficulty, so must the repairing of exploitable verifiers. To this end, we ask whether today's model with scaled compute can automatically harden agent environments to prevent potentially stronger future models from reward hacking. We introduce a scalable, fully automatic approach to weak-to-strong verifier hardening. It first sets up an isolated verifier sandbox that agents cannot directly modify, then uses a hacker-fixer loop to find and repair remaining verifier vulnerabilities.
  We apply this loop to Terminal Bench, KernelBench, and SETA, substantially reducing attack success across these agent environments. The iterative design scales with the hardening budget, producing progressively stronger defenses as the number of loop iterations increases and outperforming the static, non-iterative baseline. An earlier version of our hacker-fixer loop has been adopted by the official Terminal Bench repository as a way to audit exploits in its environments. Project page: https://verifier-hardening.github.io/.

title: Layer-wise Input Recoverability in Deep Neural Networks
summary: The inner workings of deep neural networks are still not well understood. The information bottleneck framework, which characterizes deep networks by the mutual information between their hidden representations and the network's input, has been used to identify compression of input information with respect to an input image and output labels. We instead study how much of a layer's own input is recoverable from the layer's output in convolutional neural networks (CNNs). A convolutional layer applies its filters to one input patch at a time, so we evaluate recoverability on sampled input patches with a reconstruction-based probe and not on the entire feature map. The probe's size thus depends on channels and kernel size and not on feature map size, which lets our method scale to deep CNNs with wide feature maps. For each layer, we compare pretrained, random, and reconstruction-optimized encoders, using linear and linear-plus-residual-MLP decoders. We measure recoverability as $R^2$ between input patches and their reconstructions on a held-out set. Across nine ImageNet CNNs, recoverability generally decreases with depth but is more consistently predicted by the compression of the layer. Learning-attributed recoverability, the difference between pretrained and random encoders, is not uniform across architectures. We introduce single-property random controls, which transfer one pretrained property onto a random encoder, and find that each control changes recoverability with a consistent sign across models: copying pretrained singular vectors tends to raise recoverability, while copying the pretrained singular-value spectrum or activation sparsity lowers it.

title: On the Geometry of Radar Waveform Design with Constraints
comment: 8 Pages, 10 figures; To be published in IEEE Transactions on Radar Systems
summary: Many optimization problems that arise in signal processing applications are based around optimizing vectors/matrices of numeric sequences. These problems are often inherently non-convex due to non-linear constraints. Such problems are frequently solved through convex relaxations of the original problem to allow for computationally simple algorithms to be leveraged, albeit with the potential for appreciable performance costs in the solution space. When the constraints of a problem can be implicitly satisfied through the structure of a Riemannian manifold, optimizing directly on said manifold affords the opportunity to solve the problem in an unconstrained fashion. Therefore, when feasible, recasting the constrained optimization problem in Euclidean space as an unconstrained optimization over a Riemannian manifold offers greater flexibility and improved efficiency over convex relaxation based approaches. This paper introduces the minimal smooth optimization theory required and adapts the notation to a radar signal design context. In addition, we apply our approach to two different problems in direct parallel to contemporary convex relaxation-based signal design literature.

title: On Measures of Dissimilarity on the Majorization Simplex
summary: The majorization simplex $\mathcal{P}_n$ is the set of probability vectors of length $n$ whose entries are arranged in non-increasing order. Under the majorization order, $\mathcal{P}_n$ is a lattice, and it is the natural space for comparing distributions when the labels of the outcomes are not relevant. In this work, we study measures of dissimilarity (and, similarity) on $\mathcal{P}_n$. Our first set of results concerns the Rényi-entropy based distance $d_α(p,q)=H_α(p)+H_α(q)-2H_α(p\vee q)$ proposed by Yadav and Shkel (2026), which generalizes a metric of Cicalese, Gargano and Vaccaro (2013). We show that $d_α$ is a metric on $\mathcal{P}_n$ for $α\in[1,\infty)$, while for $α\in[0,1)\cup\{\infty\}$, $d_α$ is not a metric in general. Our main result in this part identifies the necessary and sufficient conditions for equality in the triangle inequality of $d_α$ when $α>1$, for which we identify the equality conditions for the supermodularity of the Rényi entropy $H_α$. Our second set of results concerns the total variation distance and the Hellinger affinity (also called the Bhattacharyya coefficient) on $\mathcal{P}_n$. We obtain a number of bounds on these measures, along with some of their equality conditions. The resulting Hellinger affinity based upper bound on the total variation distance can be smaller than the bounds obtained from Pinsker's and the Bretagnolle--Huber inequalities.

title: Filtering for Liveness: Recurrence via Backup Reachability Control Barrier Functions
summary: Liveness requires a dynamical system to repeatedly accomplish a desired objective over time. In this work, we consider a particular form of liveness known as recurrence, which requires the closed-loop trajectory to regularly revisit a prescribed set, with no more than a specified amount of time between visits. Inspired by the control barrier function (CBF) safety-filter paradigm, we develop a controller-filtering framework that makes adjustments to a nominal controller only when necessary to guarantee recurrence. Unlike conventional CBF methods, which enforce set forward invariance, our framework allows the trajectory to leave the set while guaranteeing its timely return. To achieve this, our framework combines two components: a backup reachability CBF that preserves the ability to return to the prescribed set within the allowable time, and a timing-based mechanism that invokes a reaching controller only when the nominal behavior would otherwise fail to meet the return-time requirement. The resulting framework guarantees recurrence while preserving the nominal behavior when possible, enabling control objectives that require temporary excursions from the set, such as traversal between disjoint regions. Our method is successfully utilized in a drone racing example with a recurrence constraint on beacon visibility.

title: Hardware-Assisted Multi-Stage Ransomware Detection with Adaptive Machine Learning
summary: Ransomware is a fast-escalating privacy threat causing significant financial and data losses worldwide. As attacks grow more sophisticated, traditional static signatures and dynamic behavior analysis struggle to defend. In this paper, we propose an novel framework that couples software-level scanning with hardware-level microprocessor activity monitoring to achieve efficient ransomware detection and mitigation. The contributions are threefold: (1) we employ adversarial training to harden static analysis against obfuscation and leverage hardware-assisted monitoring for real-time detection; (2) we integrate neural architecture search (NAS) to automatically tailor models for stronger generalizability; and (3) We validate the proposed approach through extensive experiments, demonstrating substantially improved detection accuracy and reduced latency compared with existing methods. Moreover, it provides trace-level interpretability that explains the underlying decision process.

title: Learning to See through Action: Predictive Curiosity for Robots
summary: Humans and animals do not learn vision from a fixed set of data: they move, interact, and learn from the visual consequences of their actions. Motivated by this developmental view, we study whether robots can improve visual learning by actively collecting experience through curiosity-driven interaction. We introduce DySCOVER, a self-supervised framework for active robot visual learning. A robot observes RGB frames, learns a visual autoencoder that encodes and reconstructs them, and trains a recurrent world model to predict the next visual latent state conditioned on the current state and action. The agent's policy is trained only with intrinsic rewards: reconstruction error encourages visually novel observations, while the world model's error encourages transitions whose consequences are not yet predictable. This prediction error biases the policy toward more intricate trajectories that enrich the agent's set of experiences with observations beyond those encouraged by visual novelty alone. Our experiments conducted with robotic arms as the embodied agents show that adding predictive curiosity improves the vision model over using visual curiosity alone. Across variations in initial conditions, experience capacity, embodiment, and scene content, adding predictive curiosity consistently improved visual learning. These results show that predictive curiosity can improve active visual learning beyond reconstruction-based curiosity alone.

title: Optimal Gating for Dead-Time-Constrained Single-Photon Detectors
summary: We develop a Fisher-information framework for optimizing single-photon detector gating in periodic experiments, in contrast to previous more empirical or heuristic gating choices. After each photon detection, such a detector is insensitive for a dead time, so that an early background detection can obscure a later signal. Gating preserves availability for informative photons by selectively deactivating the detector. In our high-pile-up simulation of distance-attenuated lidar, our practical data-independent gating design reduces the worst-case asymptotic range variance by more than half relative to the free-running acquisition (which does not use any gating). More generally, we characterize achievable detector-active frequencies as a convex polytope and construct an adaptive rule that asymptotically attains an optimal "oracle" design without prior knowledge of the physical parameters. We also derive practical criteria that quantify the potential gains of gating and/or photon attenuation over unattenuated free-running acquisition.

title: Universal Distributed Feature Extraction Complementary to Side Information via H-Score
summary: This paper considers a distributed estimation system where edge nodes transmit averaged features to a center node for parameter estimation. A key challenge arises when the center node possesses auxiliary side information: how to design local extractors that are universally optimal for any downstream task, while avoiding redundancy with the side information. To tackle this problem, we orthogonally decompose the joint function space and demonstrate in the weak-dependence regime that the modal decomposition of the canonical dependence kernel's conditional-additive component yields optimal, task-independent features. We construct a distributed nested H-score to learn this decomposition and show that, under a limited feature budget, the mean-squared error (MSE) gap to the best task-specific features is determined solely by the task's alignment with the discarded, least informative modes, and vanishes to leading order for every square-integrable task once the budget is sufficient.

title: Direct Electromechanical Actuation of the Shift Drum in Non-Synchronized Motorcycle Transmissions: From Actuator Sizing and Electronics Design to Closed-Loop Position Control
comment: Original German title (2019): Entwickeln eines automatisierten Schaltgetriebes fuer Motorraeder. Diploma thesis, Westsaechsische Hochschule Zwickau, 2019; revised English edition 2026. 73 pages, 30 figures, 15 tables. Firmware and shift time dataset: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23002655)
summary: This thesis presents the direct electromechanical actuation of the shift drum in a non-synchronized motorcycle transmission. A DC motor drives the shift drum through a self-locking worm gear, so the entire foot shift mechanism is eliminated. As a reference, 84 manual gear changes of a large-displacement series-production motorcycle were measured on a chassis dynamometer; the mean shift time is 80 ms for upshifts and 92 ms for downshifts. The system design covers the complete chain from the mechanics to the software. The actuator motor is sized from inertia, friction and gear ratio. A dedicated shift controller is developed with supply filtering, signal conditioning for the position sensor and the incremental encoder, an H-bridge motor driver and a custom circuit board based on a SAMD21 microcontroller. The embedded firmware implements position control of the shift drum with a proportional controller, without inner speed or current loops. On a gearbox test rig, a gear change is completed in less than 80 ms without overshoot in a single measurement, below the mean of the manual reference shifts. The analysis reveals a trade-off in the choice of the worm gear ratio: at a ratio of 30, about 93% of the motor torque is needed to accelerate the motor shaft and the worm. A ratio of about 8 halves the required torque, but the worm gear then loses its self-locking. The measured shift times are published as an open dataset.

title: CreepScope: Measuring Post-Use Authorization Exposure in Tool-Using Agents
summary: Authorization checks at individual tool calls do not reveal how long earlier authority remains usable. We study this lifecycle failure as privilege creep: a capability stays reachable after its last justified workflow step. We present CreepScope, a trace-oriented evaluation protocol that samples reachable authority at every step and separates no-remaining-use exposure into stale-after-use and never-required components; Capability-Step Exposure (CSE) counts total stepwise overexposure and Residual Privilege Debt (RPD) the terminal residue, while stale-after-use exposure is the direct privilege-creep measure. A 96-cell deterministic replay over 12 controlled storage, communication, and cloud-operation workflows validates these semantics: Static Task Scope and Monotonic On-Demand retain mean CSEs of 26 and 13, whereas an oracle-controlled Step Lease has zero CSE and zero residual debt by construction. All three persistent regimes share the same stale-after-use exposure of 13, so their CSE differences come from scope and grant timing rather than post-use retention; Full Access alone adds 91.33 never-required capability-steps. A separate 24-episode local case then lets Qwen2 7B choose tools in one simulated mail workflow: the injected stale send executes in all nine persistent-policy episodes and in none of the three Step-Lease episodes, while all 24 required action sequences complete. These results establish a reproducible containment case, not cross-workflow or cross-model effectiveness. Core metrics are reconstructed from raw events, and exact gates reject incomplete or duplicated evaluation grids.

title: Decentralized Bandit Learning of Markov Perfect Equilibria
summary: We study decentralized bandit learning in discounted infinite-horizon, general-sum Markov games with continuous actions. Agents observe the public state, but only their own realized rewards, and use simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation to update their actions. Under strong monotonicity of the negative running-reward gradients and sufficiently small time steps, we prove that the fully decentralized procedure converges almost surely to the unique stationary Markov perfect equilibrium. We obtain an $O(n^{-1/2})$ convergence rate and present a natural extension to episodic finite-horizon learning.

title: Energy-Efficient RF Chain Activation for Uplink mmWave Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems: A Minimum-Cost Maximum-Flow Approach
comment: Accepted for presentation at 2026 IEEE Globecom Workshops (GC Wkshps)
summary: With the incessant demand for green and sustainable communications, energy efficiency (EE) has become a cornerstone of sixth-generation (6G) network design, especially for cell-free millimeter-wave (mmWave) massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems, which can achieve significant throughput gains by leveraging large-scale antenna arrays. Adaptive radio frequency (RF) chain activation (ARFA) is a key technique for reducing power consumption without severely degrading the achievable rate, thereby enhancing the total EE of 6G MIMO systems. In this paper, we propose a minimum-cost maximum-flow (MCMF)-based ARFA scheme to reduce unnecessary power consumption and maximize the total EE of uplink mmWave cell-free massive MIMO systems. Simulation results indicate that the proposed approach can significantly improve the total EE while maintaining a relatively high achievable rate and acceptable computational complexity.

title: Digital-Twin-Referenced Belief-Guided Q-Learning for Jammer Identification and Beam-Power Control in a mmWave Model
summary: Digital Twin (DT) combined with reinforcement learning (RL) can support adaptive resource allocation and security-aware decision-making by comparing expected and observed network behavior. This paper presents a simulation-based DT reference and a belief-guided Q-learning (BGQL) for joint jammer identification and beam-power control in a site-specific 28-GHz network. For each action, the same channel simulator is evaluated under an attack-free and an attacked configuration. Receiver-level residuals are combined with spatial jamming footprints and accumulated to form a normalized suspicion vector. BGQL incorporates this vector into an aggregated state, a belief-concentration reward, and exploratory beam-selection rule. The BGQL scheme is compared with SARSA, Greedy, and Random under matched attacker sets. Across 30 paired Monte Carlo runs in four configurations, with the number of active jammers supplied to every method, BGQL achieves mean aggregate full-band link-rate scores of approximately 437.4--564.2~Mbit/s and rate-to-device-power scores of 60.37--76.79~Mbit/J. Its detection accuracy is 100\% in one-jammer configurations and approximately 78\%--81\% in two-jammer configurations. BGQL requires approximately 80--130~s per run, compared with 5--14~s for SARSA, reflecting evaluation of 625 beam pairs during exploratory steps. These findings provide a matched-model simulation proof of concept for DT-referenced belief-guided learning for security-aware beam-power control in 6G networks.

title: Input-Constrained Active Disturbance Rejection Control for AUVs
summary: This paper addresses the control of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) operating in dynamic environments, where wave-induced forces, modelling errors, and actuator limitations make reliable control challenging. Active disturbance rejection control (ADRC), together with an extended state observer (ESO), estimates lumped uncertainties online, simplifying control design using nominal models. However, existing stability analyses typically assume bounded control inputs and derivatives, which are difficult to guarantee under unknown disturbances and measurement noise. To bridge this theory--practice gap, this paper introduces an ADRC framework with active input saturation and post-saturation low-pass filtering. The saturation constrains the control magnitude, while the filter regularizes the saturated signal to ensure bounded input-rate variations. By explicitly enforcing these conditions, the proposed system guarantees semi-global practical asymptotic stability. High-fidelity simulations and experiments on an underwater robotic platform demonstrate robust control performance under severe environmental disturbances and actuator constraints. A supplementary video is available at https://youtu.be/AEFlZ69Yg00.

title: AutoSec-RAN: Specification-Grounded LLM Fine-Tuning for Automated Security Analysis of O-RAN
comment: This paper has been accepted in The 14th IEEE Conference on Communications and Network Security (IEEE CNS 2026)
summary: This paper presents AutoSec-RAN, a specification-grounded large language model (LLM) framework for automated security triage of Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) testing. Unlike approaches relying on static rule sets or privileged access to raw packet captures, AutoSec-RAN fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct through two Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) stages over a curated corpus of 69 O-RAN, 3GPP, and adjacent standards documents, then selectively augments inference with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over the same specification index. At inference, the model receives only an investigator-style question and a scenario metadata block, simulating an automated analyst operating without raw packet evidence. AutoSec-RAN is validated on a purpose-built 5G/O-RAN testbed across labeled fronthaul distributed denial of service replay scenarios. A Gemma-4-31B judge LLM scores each candidate's answer on faithfulness, correctness, and actionability relative to a reference authored from full packet capture and log evidence. AutoSec-RAN achieves a mean judge overall score of 0.713 across all 313 evaluation items (0.755 restricted to the five supervised taxonomy classes), clearing the 0.70 reporting threshold, and a blended score of 0.778 (0.808 supervised-only) when cosine similarity over Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence (BAAI) General Embedding (BGE) is incorporated as a secondary semantic signal.
