The framework performs strongest on mitigation and threat-model reasoning (with a mean overall of 0.849 and 0.848, respectively) and identifies a measurable gap on the held-out attack-direction class (0.515), a controlled result that exposes a specific training data requirement. These results establish specification-grounded LoRA fine-tuning combined with RAG retrieval as a viable foundation for automated security validation of AI-native O-RAN.

title: Continuous-Time Cloth Dynamics with Physics-Informed Neural ODEs
summary: We present ContinuousCloth, a continuous-time, physics-informed neural solver for deformable cloth dynamics that enforces a spring--mass ODE within a neural trajectory model. Unlike classical time-stepping simulators that return trajectories only on a discrete integration grid, ContinuousCloth supports querying at arbitrary timestamps and computing displacement, velocity, and acceleration via automatic differentiation. We evaluate ContinuousCloth along two dimensions. In a physics-only setting, ContinuousCloth achieves trajectory accuracy comparable to high-precision solvers across six diverse boundary-condition scenarios while reducing runtime by up to 17.4 times. When fused with sparse and noisy observations, the spring--mass ODE acts as a strong inductive bias for downstream tasks: interpolation and parameter estimation. That is, ContinuousCloth reduces interpolation error by 7.3 times over a data-only neural baseline in simulation and 2.4 times on real-world cloth sequences, and achieves 2.6 times lower parameter error than a differentiable-solver baseline under high-noise conditions, demonstrating consistent robustness under realistic measurement imperfections.

title: Timing Misalignment and Its Impact on OTFS and Other Delay-Based Waveforms
comment: Published in: IEEE Transactions on Communications. Date of Publication: 01 September 2026. Volume: 74. Page(s): 13657 - 13671. no ISSUE number is shown yet
summary: The shift towards 6G wireless networks calls for advanced waveforms to support emerging applications such as ultra-reliable and massive machine-type communications. Among the proposed candidates, OTFS, ODDM, OTSM, and OCDM share the common feature of exploiting the delay domain for data transmission. While these waveforms offer significant advantages in high-mobility and sensing scenarios, their integration into multi-user uplink systems reveals a critical challenge: timing misalignment (TM). Unlike OFDM, where residual timing offsets translate into phase rotations, delay-based waveforms experience actual shifts of resources, whose impact we investigate in this work. We show that the aforementioned waveforms can be unified under a time-invariant setup through a common input--output relation, which enables a unified analysis of TM in uplink resource allocation. The results reveal a fundamental trade-off between interference mitigation and guard overhead in the presence of TM. We further benchmark the observed behavior against OFDM under Doppler spread as a reference impairment and highlight the analogy between TM in delay-based allocation and Doppler spread in frequency-based allocation. The results show that delay-based waveforms can maintain a net performance advantage over OFDM in the considered setup. Beyond this unified Doppler-free analysis, we evaluate the joint impact of Doppler spread and TM on each waveform individually. We also investigate BER performance and show how coding can mitigate the resulting interference. This study therefore establishes a problem framework that motivates the development of future compensation and scheduling strategies for practical multi-user operation of delay-based waveforms.

title: Information-Theoretic Limits for Rectangular Spiked Matrix Models with Rotationally Invariant Noise
summary: We study the information-theoretic limits of inference in rectangular rank-one spiked matrix models with additive rotationally invariant noise, thereby going beyond the standard assumption of independent noise entries. Using the replica method from statistical physics, we derive a variational formula for the mutual information between the signal and the data, together with a system of saddle point equations predicting the minimum mean squared error in estimating the rank-one spike. We further show that, in the Bayes-optimal setting, these saddle point equations coincide with the fixed point equations of the state evolution of a recently proposed orthogonal approximate message passing algorithm with Bayes-optimal denoisers. This equivalence provides an algorithmic interpretation of the replica prediction and supports the Bayes-optimality of orthogonal approximate message passing whenever the relevant fixed point is unique. Numerical evaluations of the saddle point equations for several rotationally invariant noise ensembles and signal priors, together with finite-size simulations of the algorithm, confirm the asymptotic predictions. They illustrate both regimes with a unique informative fixed point, where orthogonal approximate message passing is predicted to attain the minimum mean squared error, and regimes with multiple fixed points, where a statistical-to-computational gap exists.

title: Multi-Day Stochastic Dispatch for Power Systems With Long-Duration Storage Using Diffusion-Generated Weather Forecasts
summary: As power systems shift toward high shares of wind and solar, long-duration storage becomes pivotal for balancing multi-day deficits and surpluses of uncertain supply and demand. Current dispatch strategies for long-duration storage either assign a fixed value to stored energy or extend the modeled horizon using a single forecast. Stochastic system dispatch with a multi-day horizon for long-duration storage remains unexplored, and existing stochastic dispatch only considers day-ahead uncertainty or Markovian uncertainty beyond one week of perfect foresight. Therefore, we benchmark stochastic multi-day dispatch against deterministic alternatives in a rolling-horizon setup. To emulate probabilistic multi-day forecasts, we combine diffusion with a semi-Markov model of weather regimes and a logistic growth model for meteorological forecast errors. At high renewable shares, stochastic operation reduces thermal backup generation and consistently eliminates loss of load. The benefits decrease with smaller shares of renewables, less long-duration storage, or higher forecast skill. Overall, our results suggest that systems with high shares of variable renewables can substantially benefit from probabilistic multi-day forecasts and stochastic dispatch.

title: DelegateGuard: Purpose-Bound Capabilities for Delegated LLM Agent Workflows
summary: \textbf{(Context)} LLM agents increasingly delegate subtasks while holding authority over sensitive data, creating confused-deputy risks: an injected delegate can exfiltrate data, amplify its authority, or act after revocation. Existing leakage benchmarks expose these failures but do not constrain the authority a delegated agent may exercise. \textbf{(Methods)} We present \system, a reference monitor that converts the initiating user's authorization into attenuable capabilities over purpose, labels, operations, sinks, and delegation depth; every data-moving action is mediated outside the LLM, and revocation cascades through the delegation graph. We formalize a trace-level safety invariant and evaluate it with an adaptive within-authority adversary and four baselines, model-action and multi-turn ecological studies, and conformance and scale checks over deterministic traces and 517{,}401 Enron emails. \textbf{(Results)} \system blocks ungranted-sink exfiltration, authority amplification, revocation replay, purpose gaming, and intra-tool label violations, and dominates static allowlists on the revocation and intra-tool cases (10/10). Two open models proposed attacker-goal actions on 42/45 and 44/45 injected traces, all blocked at execution; a 90-run multi-turn study cut leakage from 0.844 to 0.20 with full task completion, at microsecond per-decision overhead. Proposition~1 characterizes exactly where attenuation-based authorization suffices, a boundary we also reproduce empirically across four observable-sink workflows. \textbf{(Conclusion \& Significance)} Purpose-bound runtime authorization gives delegated LLM workflows a model-independent execution boundary and a precise recipe for composing it with declassification and content monitoring on externally observable sinks.

title: On the Depth Transfer of Neural Optimizers via L-Smoothness
summary: Scaling deep learning models efficiently requires predictable performance transfer across compute regimes. Establishing reliable hyperparameter transfer allows optimal training dynamics and structural choices to be discovered on low-cost proxy models, avoiding catastrophic failures during massive-scale training. Existing depth-transfer analyses are architecture-specific and heuristic: hyperparameter transfer is only justified through toy blocks, and both rely on infinite-depth dynamics, a specific initialization, and feature-learning criteria. Building on $L$-smoothness framework of Xu et al. (2026), we understand hyperparameter transfer as how do the Lipschitz and $L$-smoothness constants of the loss scale with the depth $K$? We show that inverse-depth residual branch scaling $α=Θ(1/K)$ is sufficient to make both constants depth-independent at fixed width, uniformly over the bounded parameter domain and for arbitrary $p\to q$ geometries. Because the bounds depend on each residual branch only through its Lipschitz and smoothness constants, the argument applies to general residual networks (including branches of block depth $\geq 2$ such as transformer and ResNet blocks) without assumptions on initialization or correlations between layer weights. Since the smoothness constant controls the curvature penalty in the descent inequality, our bounds motivate a learning-rate scale without an additional depth-dependent curvature correction for updates bounded in the prescribed norm. This provides a geometric explanation of inverse-depth residual scaling and its application to the operator-norm geometries associated with AdamW, Muon, and MOGA. Learning-rate sweeps on GPT-2 (depths 2--128) and CIFAR-100 ResNets (8--32 residual blocks) confirm that Muon and MOGA exhibit stable learning-rate transfer under these prescriptions, with a common optimal rate across a 64-fold increase in depth.

title: Learning or Modeling? Virtual XL-RIS Observation Reconstruction for Near-Field Sensing
summary: A passive extremely large-scale reconfigurable intelligent surface (XL-RIS) offers a position-sensitive aperture for near-field sensing, but its element-wise signals are not directly observed. Recovering this virtual RIS observation (VOR) from fewer base-station measurements requires prior information. This paper investigates when calibrated propagation geometry or paired training data provides the more effective reconstruction prior. For a common sensing operator and target signal, we develop off-grid near-field sparse parametric reconstruction (OG-NF-SPR) and compare it with compact and DenseNet-based deep reconstructors. OG-NF-SPR uses reflected-path projection for position initialization, followed by Bayesian estimation of all path gains and continuous position refinement. A causal extension incorporates temporal correlation without trajectory labels. Controlled simulations use near-field UAV tracking as an illustration and separately examine noise, position-distribution shift, calibration error, and propagation mismatch. Under matched propagation at 20 dB, OG-NF-SPR achieves approximately 67% lower reconstruction NMSE than the two nominal deep networks. At low SNR, statistical averaging is more effective than selecting a single geometric explanation. Under sufficiently strong repeatable mismatch, a same-size network trained on the mismatch family outperforms the nominal physical estimator, whereas nominal training does not provide this benefit. Temporal regularization also reduces position RMSE from 0.653 m to 0.225 m on a shared trajectory. The results relate reconstruction performance to measurement quality, calibration accuracy, and training coverage, providing guidance on when geometry can replace supervised labels and when additional data are useful.

title: On the Multi-Weight Shift-Sum Iterative Decoding of Short BCH Codes
summary: This paper investigates a shift-sum decoding algorithm that employs dual codewords. Existing dual codeword shift-sum decoding schemes mainly rely on minimum-weight dual codewords. However, the number of such codewords is often limited, which restricts the amount of reliability information available to the decoder. To address this issue, we extend the component counting mechanism from minimum-weight dual codewords to dual codewords whose Hamming weights lie within a prescribed upper bound. We further introduce a normalized component counting rule to suppress the overcounting bias caused by the much larger populations of higher-weight classes. Based on this framework, we develop a hard-decision iterative error reduction decoder and a soft information-aided iterative error reduction decoder. Numerical results show that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing minimum-weight shift-sum baselines especially for short codes where additional dual codeword information is particularly valuable.

title: A Collision-Aware Predictive Rerouting Framework for Connected and Automated Vehicles
summary: In this paper, we investigate the problem of mitigating non-recurrent congestion in urban transportation networks through predictive and adaptive routing for connected and automated vehicles (CAVs). We propose a collision-aware predictive rerouting framework that integrates microscopic SUMO simulation, DCRNN-based spatiotemporal traffic-state forecasting, collision-window lookahead, and multi-objective route scoring. The routing controller uses predicted congestion, live emission information, route-length penalties, and incident-window constraints to decide when CAVs deviate from their current routes. The completed simulation campaign across three urban network scenarios, five CAV penetration levels, three random seeds, and multiple benchmark rerouting strategies shows that the proposed full framework does not dominate all baselines in aggregate travel time, distance, or emissions. Instead, its principal advantage is operational stability: it maintains comparable network-level efficiency while substantially reducing rerouting frequency relative to active rerouting baselines. These results demonstrate both the promise and the tradeoffs of embedding graph-based prediction and collision awareness into real-time CAV rerouting, and they motivate further work on forecast calibration, uncertainty-aware prediction, and system-level fairness between CAV and non-CAV traffic.

title: Adversarial Robustness of Camera-Radar Sensor Fusion for Autonomous Driving
summary: Autonomous driving (AD) relies on multi-sensor perception to interpret the surrounding environment. However, the robustness of camera--radar fusion under adversarial conditions remains largely unexplored. This paper presents a systematic measurement study of the robustness of camera--radar sensor fusion in AD. We construct a unified evaluation pipeline on the nuScenes dataset that simulates attacks on both sensing modalities, including eight camera-image perturbations and three radar point-cloud perturbations. We evaluate five camera--radar fusion algorithms across two perception tasks, 3D object detection and depth estimation, and quantify their performance under clean and attacked inputs using standard metrics. Our evaluation reveals a clear asymmetry in the robustness of fusion systems. Camera perturbations substantially degrade both object detection and depth estimation, and moderate attack strengths are already sufficient to cause severe performance degradation. In contrast, the evaluated radar perturbations produce smaller and task-dependent effects, with object-detection models showing particularly limited degradation. Our analysis attributes this difference to the strong dependence of existing fusion architectures on dense camera features, together with the filtering, association, and confidence-weighting mechanisms commonly applied to sparse radar measurements. These results demonstrate that sensor fusion does not inherently guarantee robustness and that the contribution and reliability of each sensing modality must be explicitly considered under adversarial conditions. Based on four empirical findings, we derive measurement-guided design implications for future robust camera--radar fusion, including modality-specific reliability estimation, cross-modal consistency checking, adaptive fusion, and graceful failover under severe sensor degradation.

title: Class-Conditional Conformal Prediction for Signal Temporal Logic Inference with Many Classes
summary: Signal Temporal Logic (STL) inference provides interpretable formulas for time series classification. For multiclass classification, however, accurate predictions do not necessarily ensure that the inferred formulas are satisfied consistently with the true class. We introduce the positive satisfaction rate and codeword satisfaction rate to quantify satisfaction of required formulas and consistency with the complete class codeword, respectively. We develop a two-stage procedure that first learns discriminative formulas using a margin-based objective and then refines predicate thresholds toward a small positive robustness target while fixing the formula structure and temporal intervals. Satisfaction and ranking penalties discourage violations of required formulas and loss of class separation. The decoding loss is used as a nonconformity score and calibrated separately for each class, providing finite-sample class-conditional coverage under intra-class exchangeability. Experiments on naval, synthetic, and robot manipulation trajectories demonstrate discrepancies between classification accuracy and formula satisfaction. The results further reveal a data-dependent tradeoff between robustness tightness and satisfaction, while class-conditional calibration mitigates undercoverage that can be hidden by pooled calibration.

title: Shuf-Scatter: Permutation-Based DLI Suppression for OFDM Ambient Backscatter
summary: Direct Link Interference (DLI) remains a major bottleneck in Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM)-based Ambient Backscatter Communication (AmBC) systems. This letter proposes Shuf-Scatter, a scheme that applies a deterministic permutation to the reflected OFDM waveform to create a distinct correlation-domain signature. By exploiting the quasi-orthogonality between the reshuffled backscatter signal and the direct-link component, the proposed receiver effectively mitigates DLI and enables reliable detection without requiring dedicated spectral resources, or instantaneous Backscatter-Link (BL) Channel State Information (CSI). Analytical and simulation results demonstrate that Shuf-Scatter achieves superior Bit Error Rate (BER) performance under strong DLI while preserving the integrity of the legacy OFDM transmission.

title: The Right to Be Forgotten under Correlation: Privacy-Utility Tradeoffs
summary: We study privacy-preserving algorithms that redact information from a correlated dataset. The goal is to reduce the information leakage about sensitive parts. We analytically characterize the optimal tradeoff between privacy (leakage through correlation) and utility (number of redactions) for local mechanisms and binary Markovian correlations. Our result shows how to decompose the mechanism design problem into a sequence of local mechanism design problems and reveals their sequential relation. The optimal mechanism is the solution to a Finite-Horizon Deterministic Markov Decision Process.

title: Stability Transfer for Autonomous Systems via Higher-Order Taylor-Truncated Lyapunov Certificates
summary: We develop analytical sufficient conditions for certifying the local asymptotic stability of nonlinear autonomous systems based on Lyapunov functions derived from their finite-order Taylor polynomial approximations. This approach translates the stability analysis problem from the original nonlinear dynamics to a more computationally tractable polynomial domain. The derived conditions allow for the explicit calculation of a guaranteed inner approximation of the region of attraction ($\mathrm{ROA}$). We show how sum-of-squares (SOS) programming and grid search can be used to systematically search for polynomial Lyapunov functions that yield a large certified threshold radius and extract a certified invariant set inner approximation of the $\mathrm{ROA}$ of the nonpolynomial original system. The framework is then applied to a control tuning problem: finding reduced-effort Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) controllers that ensure that a given initial state of interest belongs to the certified $\mathrm{ROA}$ of the nonpolynomial closed loop system. The effectiveness of the overall methodology is demonstrated using a pendulum with nonlinear damping and a nonlinear control system.

title: When Agents Talk, Secrets Travel: Topology-Driven Leakage and Recipient-Conditioned Sanitization in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
summary: Multi-agent LLM systems (MALS) introduce a privacy-leakage problem that conventional sensitivity-based defenses miss, since information disclosed to one authorized agent can propagate through routine coordination to an unauthorized one, without compromise or malicious behavior. This motivates topology-aware enforcement that blocks unauthorized propagation while preserving authorized disclosure. We evaluate 485 scenarios across coordinator-worker, peer-to-peer, and hierarchical topologies, instrumenting seven communication channels and measuring surface leakage and disclosure to topology-introduced recipients. We introduce RECONS, a Detect -> Decide -> Transform sanitizer conditioning intervention on recipient and execution context rather than sensitivity alone. Topology changes where protected information propagates, with disclosure to topology-introduced recipients rising from 0% to 52.2% while surface leakage stays nearly flat at 60.6-62.8%. This effect persists across four generator models and a second orchestration framework, though magnitude and relay paths differ; framework choice separately drives a 150x leakage spread, so topology alone is not sufficient. RECONS reduces residual disclosure from 96.7% without sanitization to 29.25%, preserving 94.1% of authorized disclosures versus 20.5% under blanket redaction. Detection coverage is the dominant bottleneck, accounting for 95.5% of residual disclosures. These results show that privacy enforcement in MALS must reason about the recipient and communication path realized at runtime, not sensitivity or topology assumptions alone.

title: The Sample Complexity of Multicalibration with an ERM Oracle
summary: A predictor is multicalibrated with respect to a class of subpopulations (formally, of functions on the inputs, called auditors) if, for every subpopulation in the class and every value the predictor outputs, the average outcome among the members of that subpopulation who receive that value is close to the value itself. For finite classes, about $\varepsilon^{-3}$ samples are necessary and sufficient to learn a predictor with multicalibration error $\varepsilon$, but the algorithms that attain this rate enumerate the class, which is impossible for the large classes of interest. We ask how many samples suffice when the learner accesses the class only through an empirical risk minimization (ERM) oracle. We give an algorithm that uses $\tilde{O}(d/\varepsilon^{3})$ samples and polynomially many ERM calls, where $d$ is the VC dimension of the class. Its dependence on $\varepsilon$ is optimal for all learners. When $d$ is at least about $1/\varepsilon$, every learner that can only access the class through polynomially many ERM calls needs $\tildeΩ(d/\varepsilon^{3})$ samples. Learners with unlimited computation need only $\tilde{O}(\varepsilon^{-3}+d\varepsilon^{-2})$ samples, so the extra factor $1/\varepsilon$ on the dimension term is the price of oracle efficiency. For swap multicalibration, which allows a different function from the class for each predicted value, $\tildeΘ(d/\varepsilon^{3})$ samples are necessary and sufficient. For estimating the error of a given predictor, the ordinary notion is the harder one: the swap error can be estimated with an ERM oracle, whereas the ordinary error is NP-hard to approximate even for classes with linear-time ERM. Consequently, there are classes for which it is computationally easier to learn a multicalibrated predictor than to compute the multicalibration error of a given predictor.

title: Link Both Views: Cross-Image Routing Attention for Dual-Endpoint V2I Beam-Pair Power Prediction
summary: For sensing-aided communications, single-endpoint sensing offers only a partial view of propagation, motivating link-centric sensing across both endpoints. We propose cross-image routing attention (CIRA) for sparse association and mutual enhancement of propagation-relevant features from dual-endpoint RGB images. Building on CIRA, CiFormer predicts millimeter-wave (mmWave) beam-pair power matrices for vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) communications. Experiments show that CiFormer reduces mean absolute error and improves top-1 beam-pair selection accuracy by 3.15 percentage points over the strongest baseline. Visualizations and ablation studies support dual-endpoint sensing and selective cross-view interaction in capturing propagation-relevant dependencies, suggesting broader applications in wireless tasks beyond beam prediction.

title: Puncturing-inclusion constructions of optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes using semifield codes
summary: Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes are essential components of the multilevel construction of constant dimension codes for random network coding. This paper aims to construct optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes, focusing on the diagram \([3,3,3,5]\) with rank distance \(3\). We construct an optimal \([[3,3,3,5],6,3]_q\) Ferrers diagram rank-metric code for every prime power \(q\), thereby answering an open problem posed by Etzion et al. in 2016~\cite{Etzion2016}. The construction first builds a \([3\times4,4,3]_q\) MRD code and then proves that the Delsarte dual of its puncturing on the last column contains a \([3\times3,3,3]_q\) MRD code, which comes from semifield codes. We further construct optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes for two infinite families of Ferrers diagrams: the first relies on the \([[3,3,3,5],6,3]_q\) construction and holds for every prime power \(q\), while the second is binary and obtained directly by the puncturing-inclusion construction.

title: Constrained Grid-Forming Control for Photovoltaic Systems: A Control Barrier Function Approach
summary: This paper leverages control barrier functions (CBFs) to systematically account for constraints of voltage source converters (VSCs) and photovoltaic (PV) resources in grid-forming (GFM) control. The proposed control combines (unconstrained) dual-port GFM control with control barrier functions (CBFs) to ensure reliable and safe operation of a GFM PV system under grid faults, sudden changes in irradiance, and load perturbations. First, CBFs are used to encode physical and operational limits of the PV system, namely current and voltage limits at its ac and dc terminals. Then, CBFs are used to restrict the dynamics of dual-port GFM control to within the VSC and PV limits during both transient and steady states. To this end, a cost function is defined that encodes trade-offs between forming the ac voltage phase angle/frequency and voltage magnitude under constraints. Then, real-time optimization is used to make the least modification, as measured by the cost function, to the (unconstrained) dual-port GFM control state to remain within the safe set encoded by the CBFs. Finally, the performance of the developed constrained GFM control is evaluated through EMT simulations in MATLAB/Simulink.

title: Confidential Error-Correcting Codes
summary: We introduce Confidential Error-correcting Codes (CECs), a new cryptographic primitive that enables reliable decoding from perturbed codewords while preserving message confidentiality. We formalize this primitive through three security properties: confidentiality, robustness, and soundness. To realize this goal, we develop a general framework for constructing CECs based on a Randomness-Security Separation (RSS) structure, which first encodes a nonce to introduce randomness and then masks the encoded payload with a pseudorandom function. Based on our RSS framework, we instantiate CECs, called Conc-CEC, using concatenated Reed-Muller and Reed-Solomon codes. The resulting Conc-CEC admits provable guarantees for all three properties. Notably, compared to PRCs (CRYPTO'24), another recent cryptographic primitive with error-correcting capability, CECs achieve significantly stronger concrete security guarantees under practical parameter settings. As a primary application of CECs, we further present CECMark, a watermarking scheme for AI-generated images. Our experiments on real-world generative image models show that CECMark consistently outperforms state-of-the-art watermarking methods, including Gaussian Shading (CVPR'24), PRCMark (ICLR'25), and T2SMark (NeurIPS'25). In particular, CECMark achieves higher robustness across all 56 evaluated perturbations and ensures a false positive rate below $10^{-5}$ without introducing side effects. Taken together, our work lays a novel cryptographic foundation for trustworthy watermarking schemes that, for the first time, unify provable security guarantees with strong practical reliability.

title: ConformalGuard: False-Positive-Controlled Action Gating for LM Classifiers
summary: Language model classifiers are increasingly deployed for high-stakes decisions such as phishing screening, content moderation, and fraud triage, yet validation-set thresholds provide no finite-sample control of deployment-time false positives. We present ConformalGuard, a model-agnostic calibration layer that wraps a fixed scoring function with finite-sample control over the rate at which legitimate inputs trigger an intervention tier. Our contribution is empirical and operational, not a new conformal theorem: zero-shot LM API scores can be coarse enough (10--11 unique values here) to make temperature scaling and isotonic regression operationally identical to raw thresholding for low-FPR action gating. We compare these methods with conformal calibration for fine-tuned BERT, Claude Sonnet 4, and GPT-4o on public email corpora. For Claude, conformal calibration reduces FPR from 0.040 to 0.008 while recall falls from 0.938 to 0.875. For deterministic GPT-4o scores, the 1% operating point is too conservative to deploy (recall 0.564); three-run stochastic averaging raises recall to 0.732 at FPR 0.005. At 2% prevalence with BERT, conformal calibration removes 25 false-positive reviews per 10,000 emails (95% CI [10, 43]). The guarantee is legitimate-event-rate control under exchangeability; discrimination, workload effects, and robustness to shift remain empirical.

title: Overcoming Catastrophic Forgetting: Continual Learning for Radar Waveform Classification
comment: 15 pages, 5 figures, 16 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
summary: Automated radar waveform recognition classifies the waveform and modulation type of a received signal. As new waveform variants appear over time, a deployed classifier must learn them without retraining from scratch. Catastrophic Forgetting occurs when learning new waveforms overwrites prior knowledge. Continual Learning (CL) methods tackle this challenge, but prior radar studies only evaluate a few methods on narrow benchmarks. Practitioners lack evidence on which method to deploy or which mechanisms are effective. This work presents the first large-scale benchmark of continual learning for radar waveform recognition. Eighteen CL methods are evaluated on a sequential ten-task problem, drawn from four public datasets spanning 54 waveforms, under task- and class-incremental (TIL, CIL) settings and single- and multi-epoch regimes. Methods that retain data from old tasks lead both TIL and CIL settings. Plain replay alone closes 77-88% of the gap between the lower and upper practical limits under TIL, but only 46-55% under CIL. The internal mechanisms of the leading methods are ablated and statistically tested to identify effective mechanisms. Each ablation is paired against its full method over n=6 training seeds, topped up to n=12 when inconclusive, and p-values are Holm-Bonferroni corrected within each method's family. Ablation results show that several mechanisms confer smaller but statistically significant gains. Combining these mechanisms improves the leading F1 score by 3.4-5.5% and 2.7-4.9% under TIL and CIL, respectively, and the combined models exceed every benchmarked method in both settings for all SNRs. These results give researchers of radar waveform classification systems a mechanism-level basis for design.

title: Distribution-Dependent Improvements of McDiarmid's Inequality via Rényi Divergence
summary: We investigate whether Rényi divergence can sharpen McDiarmid's inequality and its distribution-dependent refinement induced by KL divergence. Starting from Marton's transportation proof, we show that its transport inequality fails in general when KL divergence is replaced by Rényi divergence of order $0<α<1$. For sums of independent bounded random variables, however, the additivity of Rényi divergence allows us to adapt the argument and derive concentration bounds. For Bernoulli sums, these bounds strictly improve on the distribution-dependent bound induced by KL divergence over a range of deviation thresholds. We also establish a distribution-dependent refinement of Gilardoni's inequality relating total variation to Rényi divergence, providing explicit constants for our general concentration bounds.

title: Service-Aware Hosting Capacity Assessment of Edge Data Centers with Workload Flexibility
summary: The growing demand for edge computing, content delivery, and AI services is driving the interconnection of edge data centers (DCs) with distribution networks. Before interconnection, utilities evaluate how much DC capacity can be accommodated without violating feeder current and voltage limits. Fixed peak load representations can overlook service dependent demand patterns, cooling related facility demand, and delay tolerant computing tasks. This paper develops a hosting capacity (HC) assessment model for edge DCs with shiftable workload scheduling. Three representative types are considered: mobile edge computing (MEC), content delivery network (CDN), and AI DCs. Facility demand is modeled by combining fixed base demand, service driven demand, prescribed cooling-overhead coefficient, and a shiftable workload component. Workload execution is optimized under arrival causality, maximum delay, daily energy balance constraints, and the resulting active and reactive loads are embedded in a distribution power flow model. Compared with the baseline without load shifting, the maximum bus level HC gain on the IEEE 33-bus system reaches 4.46% for MEC DCs and 9.89% for AI DCs, while CDN case shows negligible gain under the assumed cache management windows.

title: HDKEM: Authentication Allocation for Deniable Hybrid Key Exchange
summary:
Deniable authenticated key exchange (DAKE) establishes a shared key without leaving transferable evidence that a party participated. We study DAKE protocols that authenticate each fresh session with one ring signature and show that their deniability mechanisms fall into three authentication allocations: sharing an authentication witness, hiding the signing witness under a fixed ring, or varying the verified ring between real and simulated executions. For fixed-ring protocols, witness hiding yields a necessary relation between the ring signature's witness-indistinguishability gap and the protocol's $(μ,δ)$ deniability parameters. We instantiate witness hiding in HDKEM, a three-slot hybrid that combines ML-KEM-768, X25519, and an optional pairwise information-theoretic source through a split-key PRF. HDKEM binds all public session values, including a QKD key identifier when present, into authentication and key derivation. Under the stated component models, it achieves eCK key indistinguishability, forward secrecy, and strong local deniability.
  We evaluate HDKEM with FalconRS and Gandalf. Across 2,000 primitive operations, median signing/verification times are 9.20/1.02 ms for FalconRS and 18.61/0.97 ms for Gandalf in our reference environment. In source-backed mode, the corresponding TCP-application costs are 8,607 B and 8,555 B per handshake. A separate 500-session server experiment exercises the complete FalconRS source-backed path and reports a median server time of 16.29 ms including local I/O.

title: History, Adaptation, and Hidden Gain: Two Prospective Tests of Learned Predictive Control in a Synthetic Neural Population
comment: 13 pages, 4 figures. Synthetic closed-loop neural rate-control study; code, frozen protocols and results at https://github.com/lonewolf15116/NeuroLight-AI (archived: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23263620)
summary: We study learned one-step predictive control of a synthetic population of 64 leaky integrate-and-fire neurons whose light sensitivity is scaled by a hidden factor s, using two prospective confirmations on plants simulated only after the analysis was frozen. In the first (50 plants, 11 conditions), removing the 200-ms input-output history substantially worsened a parameter-count-matched neural predictor at low and moderate gain (s = 0.6, 0.8; RMSE rose by 2.47 Hz at s = 0.6, 97.5% CI 2.43-2.51). In secondary comparisons, recursively adapted ARX had the lowest mean error of the deployable controllers in 10 of 11 conditions, tuned PI with anti-windup matched or beat the network for s >= 0.7, and training for 10,000 rather than 900 epochs lowered prediction error but worsened control. Development work suggested the network's learned action sensitivity did not track the hidden gain. A second protocol (50 new plants, 9 sensitivities, 2 noise levels) confirmed three pre-specified predictions at the primary noise level. Re-estimating a single multiplicative input gain recovered 87% (95% CI 86-88%) of the benefit of full adaptive ARX. Supplying that online estimate to the network as an extra input reduced high-gain tracking error by 1.84 Hz [1.81, 1.88]. Longer training worsened the plain network by 1.09 Hz but improved the gain-input network by 1.07 Hz, a differential of 2.16 Hz [2.13, 2.20]. Under high process noise (sigma = 2.0) the effects shrank to about 0.04 Hz or less and gain-only adaptation recovered only 24% of the adaptive-ARX benefit. In this synthetic plant, at the primary noise level, one-parameter online gain estimation accounts for most of the gap between a history-based network and full adaptive ARX, and for its prediction-control mismatch.

title: A Three-Axis Rydberg Atomic Receiver Model for Polarization-Based Direction-of-Arrival Sensing
summary: This paper develops a three-axis Rydberg atomic receiver model for direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation of the radio frequency (RF) signal source. Three nominally orthogonal RF local oscillators (LOs), each assigned a distinct frequency offset, project the weak incident RF field into resolvable complex beat coefficients in the optical readout. A beat-vector observation is obtained by adopting a response calibration mechanism that maps the coefficients onto the three axes of the Cartesian coordinate system. For a known circularly polarised RF signal, this observation induces a direction-dependent Rydberg steering vector, enabling maximum-likelihood DoA estimation. The pro posed procedure translates the Rydberg beat-vector front end into a highly sensitive RF field DoA sensor. Simulation results show that trace-level beat extraction supports the proposed DoA sensing workflow and provides a basis for comparison with a traditional vector antenna (VA) benchmark.

title: Learned Score-Based Turbo Message Passing for Channel Recovery From Spatially Compressed Measurements
summary: Hybrid beamforming (HBF) reduces the hardware cost of massive MIMO base stations, but its channel acquisition requires recovering the full spatial-domain channel from highly compressed beam-domain observations. This paper proposes a learned score-based turbo message passing (L-STMP) framework for uplink HBF channel recovery under extreme spatial compression. By deeply unfolding the turbo message-passing loop and introducing trainable calibration parameters and learnable score priors in each layer, L-STMP liberates STMP from the idealized compression-matrix requirements of right-rotational invariance, and reduces inference complexity to only several unfolded layers. In addition, to preserve dominant channel components that random discrete Fourier transform (DFT) selection may miss, we introduce precoding matrix indicator (PMI)-assisted beam selection as a low-overhead directional prior. Simulation results demonstrate that L-STMP consistently outperforms existing baselines and obtains substantial reconstruction gains under PMI-assisted compression in channel reconstruction.

title: A Programming, Robotics and Automatic Control Intervention for Secondary Education Students in Sweden and Italy
comment: This paper has 40 pages and 10 figures. Partial results have been presented at NPCW26 in Denmark and are available at https://npcw2026.compute.dtu.dk/Yamashita_npcw2026.pdf
summary: This study evaluates the AutoSTEM workshop, an intervention for secondary education that combines a serious game with PID-controlled hardware. Seven workshops were conducted across Sweden and Italy. The six Swedish workshops adopted an explicitly SDT-informed facilitation framework, while the Italian workshop followed the existing educational robotics format without a formally defined SDT facilitation protocol. Self-reports, an objective knowledge quiz, and qualitative responses were analysed using multiple site-adjusted statistical approaches. Technical-specific self-efficacy increased substantially in both conditions, with large effect sizes, while objective knowledge showed only modest, non-significant gains. No significant site-adjusted differences were found between SDT and control conditions for the primary outcomes. Perceived engagement was higher in the control condition, although this finding should be interpreted cautiously. The objective knowledge composite remained positive but non-significant across sensitivity analyses. Female participants reported smaller PID self-efficacy gains than males. Qualitative findings supported evidence of PID learning while identifying technical and pacing barriers. Overall, the results suggest that the technology-rich intervention supports competence development, regardless of SDT-informed facilitation.

title: ML-Assisted Power Side-Channel Attacks on ML Accelerators in Shared FPGAs
summary: Cloud providers offer on-demand access to Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs), and multi-tenant FPGAs let multiple users share one device to improve utilization. This sharing introduces security risks: an adversary co-located with a victim on the same FPGA can mount power side-channel attacks against the victim's Machine Learning (ML) accelerator. Prior on-chip attacks on such accelerators based on Time-to-Digital Converter (TDC) sensors have recovered only small, MNIST-scale grayscale inputs, including with ML-assisted reconstruction. This work is the first on-chip, TDC-based attack to produce full-scale color reconstructions of ImageNet-scale inputs, by combining ML-based upscaling and recoloring with TDC measurements of a remote victim's ML accelerator. We frame this as a proof-of-concept leakage study: the victim implements the first convolution layer of a CNN processing 224x224 ImageNet inputs on a shared FPGA, which we isolate to characterize the input-dependent leakage, and we quantify how much of each reconstruction reflects genuinely recovered information versus ML-generated post-processing. As a preliminary countermeasure, we study a pixel-substitution defense that replaces each pixel value, within a fixed intensity budget, with one of different Hamming Weight, producing a different TDC signature. We find that this transformation costs the victim's own model more accuracy than it costs the attacker and, because it applies the same fixed, publicly reconstructable mapping to every image, is largely defeated by an attacker retrained on the transformed data; robust defenses will require randomized or input-dependent transformations.

title: When More Memory Fails: Hidden Feasibility Holes in Dynamic Tensor Rematerialization
comment: 8 pages, 2 figures. Simulator study. Code and execution records: https://github.com/lonewolf15116/dtr-stability
summary: Dynamic Tensor Rematerialization (DTR) trains neural networks under a memory budget by evicting tensors and recomputing them on demand. A natural expectation is that a budget large enough to complete training stays sufficient when it is increased. Using DTR's reference simulator, simrd, to replay the public DTR training traces, we show that this expectation fails. We call the exceptions feasibility holes: memory budgets at which an eviction policy runs out of memory although both a smaller and a larger budget complete, a form of non-monotone feasibility. Under a written sweep protocol with dated amendments, a 0.01-step budget grid shows no such hole for DTR on any of six confirmatory traces, although unresolved timeouts prevent it from establishing monotonicity. Finer sampling finds holes on InceptionV4 (three regions) and U-Net (two regions), in addition to one on the ResNet-32 development trace. Every hole is reproduced by three repeats and by unmodified simrd. For one InceptionV4 pair (0.2343 versus 0.235 of peak memory) we trace the failure to individual allocations. The larger budget avoids one eviction at an operator where the smaller budget was 173,479 bytes short. The extra data it carries forward forces a later eviction of a tensor needed three operators afterwards, and rebuilding that tensor triggers a recomputation cascade that cannot fit. Keeping that one tensor resident under the same budget prevents the failure. The two simple score changes we tested do not remove holes across traces; both add failing budgets on some traces. All results are from simulation, with no allocator model; behaviour on GPU hardware is untested.

title: Task-evoked eye movements as candidate digital biomarkers of depression severity in adolescents and young adults
summary: Objective digital measures of depression severity could complement conventional symptom assessments and facilitate more timely clinical evaluation. Here, we investigated whether task-evoked eye movements provide interpretable behavioral markers of depression severity in adolescents and young adults. In this single-center, cross-sectional study, 155 participants aged 14--20 years completed emotional-spatial free-viewing and memory-guided recall tasks and were stratified by 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores. We examined 19 prespecified eye-movement features across six task-informed domains using covariate-adjusted ordinal-trend models. Greater depression severity was associated with lower gaze-allocation entropy (standardized $β=-0.599$), fewer inter-area switches ($β=-0.526$), longer first target-entry latency ($β=0.572$), and lower target dwell proportion ($β=-0.678$; all false-discovery-rate-adjusted $q<0.001$). Emotion-specific attentional-bias measures were not associated with severity, whereas associations involving fixation dispersion weakened after adjustment for anxiety symptoms. In a complementary machine-learning analysis incorporating 44 candidate eye-movement features and demographic covariates, a three-stage cascade classifier achieved the highest four-class stratification performance (accuracy, 0.665; macro-F1, 0.670; area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.869), outperforming single-stage and two-stage approaches. Together, these findings identify altered visual exploration and memory-guided gaze control as candidate digital biomarkers of depression severity, rather than generalized negative attentional bias. These results support further prospective evaluation of task-evoked eye tracking as a complementary approach for timely severity assessment and clinical decision support.

title: The Covering Radius of the Reed--Muller Code RM(1,9) is 242
summary: What is the covering radius of the Reed--Muller code RM(1,9) ? This is a long-standing open problem in cryptography and coding theory. In this paper, we resolve this problem, and prove that the covering radius of RM(1,9) is 242. We exclude nonlinearity 244 by obtaining a cubic Boolean function achieving a sharp Walsh $\ell^1$ bound. Its equality cases reduce either to an impossible cubic hyperplane restriction or to two homogeneous cubic forms in the Brier--Langevin classification. To exclude nonlinearity 243, we deduce the inequality ${\Vert W_g\Vert }_{1}+2|W_g(0)|\le 10368$, and then reduce either to a spectrum bounded by 24 or to the same expression to be at least 10496.

title: Safe Unicycle Navigation Among Multiple Obstacles Under Bounded Disturbances: A Learning-Augmented CLF-CBF Approach (Extended Version)
summary: This paper presents a robust control framework for safe navigation of a unicycle robot to a goal among multiple static obstacles under an unknown, time-varying disturbance. The controller solves a single real-time quadratic program (QP) that combines a goal-reaching term with one safety term per obstacle. The goal-reaching term is a cross-track control Lyapunov function built from body-frame tracking errors rather than a bearing angle, which keeps its Lie derivatives bounded everywhere, including the goal. Safety is encoded using robust control barrier functions, one per obstacle, each tightened by a closed-form, state-dependent disturbance bound. When stabilization and safety conflict, a slack variable relaxes only the convergence requirement, so that the safety constraints remain strictly enforced. Whenever the QP is feasible, the robust barrier constraints guarantee forward invariance of every obstacle's safe set under all admissible disturbances. Complementing this safety guarantee, a Lyapunov analysis yields an explicit ultimate bound on the distance to the goal. A learning-augmented variant replaces the fixed objective with a reinforcement-learning reference, which accelerates convergence when multiple constraints are simultaneously active. We further derive the obstacle separation below which the gap between two obstacles becomes too narrow to pass through under the robust constraints. For such gaps, a learned virtual goal for the Lyapunov function steers the robot around the obstacles without compromising safety. Simulations, a Monte Carlo study, and a comparison against a sampled-data robust baseline support the theoretical results.

title: ATTCK-R: Knowledge-Aware Long-Horizon Jailbreaking for Protected LLMs
summary: As large language models are deployed behind increasingly sophisticated safety mechanisms, evaluating their robustness under realistic adversarial conditions becomes increasingly difficult and critical. Existing jailbreaking evaluations often rely on static prompts, limited interaction horizons, or lightly protected systems, failing to reflect protected deployment settings with prompt-based safety protections. We show that the introduction of a prompt-based safety protection reduces the average attack success rate of a strong multi-turn baseline from 0.896 to 0.608 (32.1\% relative), demonstrating that unprotected evaluations substantially overestimate real-world vulnerabilities. We propose Adaptive Traceback and Tactic Curation for Knowledge-based Red-teaming (ATTCK-R), a planning-driven multi-turn red teaming framework designed for protected black-box systems. ATTCK-R models jailbreaking as a long-horizon trajectory optimization problem using a structured belief state, introduces optimization-based tactic curation to abstract reusable strategies from prior successes and failures, and employs informed traceback to resume attacks from strategically meaningful states rather than restarting. Evaluated across 9 widely used LLMs configured with a single prompt-based safety protection layer, ATTCK-R consistently outperforms strong recent multi-turn jailbreaking frameworks. Ablation results confirm that long-horizon planning and tactic curation improve attack effectiveness, while adaptive traceback improves efficiency through structured recovery from conversational failure.

title: DPAL: A Test-Time Adaptation Loss for Financial Time Series Forecasting
summary: Test-time adaptation (TTA) enables time series forecasters to update after deployment as new observations become available. However, adaptation objectives that focus primarily on prediction errors at individual time steps do not fully address the needs of financial time series forecasting. In addition to pointwise return fitting, return direction and the price trajectories reconstructed from sequences of returns are also important. To better account for these properties, we introduce Direction- and Price-Aware Adaptation Loss (DPAL), which combines pointwise return fitting with directional and price-calibration terms. We apply DPAL within existing TSF-TTA frameworks without modifying the source forecaster or the adapter architecture. Across a diverse collection of financial datasets, DPAL reduces reconstructed-price mean squared error in most evaluated settings.

title: Contactless gait-derived features as candidate digital biomarkers of depression severity in adolescents
summary: Timely assessment of depression severity in adolescents is essential for guiding clinical care, yet conventional evaluations rely on episodic clinical assessments and symptom rating scales. Contactless gait analysis offers a potentially scalable approach to capturing objective behavioral features associated with depression. Here, we introduce the Long-Distance 3D Adolescent Depression Gait Dataset (LD3D-ADG), comprising depth-sensor gait recordings from 119 adolescents at a single center, including 39 healthy controls, 41 with mild depression, and 39 with moderate-to-severe depression. We developed UMLPA-GCN, a graph convolutional network that models spatiotemporal gait dynamics across three anatomically defined skeletal partitions. In participant-independent five-fold cross-validation, UMLPA-GCN achieved 75.63% classification accuracy, a macro-F1 score of 75.52%, and a macro-area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.839 (95% confidence interval, 0.779--0.899). Class-specific recall was 87.18%, 63.41%, and 76.92% for healthy controls, mild depression, and moderate-to-severe depression, respectively. At the participant level, reduced arm swing, slower pelvic movement, restricted joint range of motion, and greater arm-swing asymmetry were identified as leading potential digital biomarkers contributing to depression severity assessment, associated with higher 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores. These findings provide proof-of-concept evidence for contactless digital depression severity stratification in adolescents. Further external and prospective validation is needed to establish their utility for longitudinal monitoring and timely clinical assessment.

title: The Maximum Nonlinearity of 8-variable Balanced Boolean Functions is 116
summary: Does there exist an 8-variable balanced Boolean function with nonlinearity 118? This is a famous and long-standing open problem in Boolean functions. In this paper, we give a negative answer to this open problem, and prove that the maximum nonlinearity of balanced Boolean functions in 8 variables is 116, establishing the 8-variable instance of Dobbertin's conjectured recursion for the minimum Walsh peak of balanced functions. Equivalently, the covering radius of the Reed--Muller code RM(1,8) in 0-resilient Boolean functions is 116. We deduce the result by obtaining a quadratic form of polar rank 6, and reducing the problem to the existence of a 6-variable Boolean function with nonlinearity greater than 26 whose Hamming distance to a bent function is between 4 and 6.

title: Enforcing a Strict Safety Margin in LLM Text Generation via Barrier Lyapunov Control
summary: Large language models are increasingly deployed without formal guarantees against toxic text generation. Existing control barrier function (CBF) based safety filters can keep the generation trajectory within a toxicity-free region, but do not enforce a positive distance from its boundary, allowing formally safe trajectories to approach the toxicity threshold arbitrarily closely and leaving little buffer against modelling errors or disturbances. We address this limitation with a Barrier Lyapunov Function (BLF) safety filter that enforces a prescribed clearance margin throughout generation while retaining the continuous-time transformer dynamics, including feedforward layers. The resulting safe input set is a half-space defined by a constraint affine in the control input, and is non-empty under certified surjectivity and classifier-nondegeneracy conditions. For margin-compatible initial conditions we prove that the clearance margin is never violated and that the prescribed clearance is restored exponentially, yielding an explicit clearance floor, and show that, as the margin vanishes, the admissible trajectories satisfy the exponential second-order CBF condition. We further derive an explicitly computable sufficient disturbance budget under which the clearance guarantee degrades gracefully. Simulations on a small transformer illustrate the resulting improvement in safety clearance.

title: Doctor Trigger: A Framework for Release-Bound Face Verification
summary: Face swapping and generative editing enable realistic facial manipulation, while online redistribution complicates publisher oversight of circulating face images. Existing approaches establish provenance, detect manipulation, recover embedded watermarks, verify image integrity, or disrupt unauthorized face manipulation. These capabilities do not necessarily establish consistency with a specific publisher-enrolled release, limiting the evidence available for verification and human review. To address this gap, we introduce Doctor Trigger, a framework for verifying circulating faces against private publisher-held release records. Before publication, the publisher embeds a weak keyed Fourier-phase signal in each face while preserving visual fidelity and stores its spectral reference. Afterward, verification compares the circulating face with that reference and uses key projection to measure retention of the release-specific signal. Therefore, relation and key evidence jointly help publishers identify suspicious copies for review, potentially reducing the circulation of manipulated images. Experimental results across FF++, DFDC, and Celeb-DF show that spectral agreement separates tested face swaps and generative manipulations from enrolled releases, while the keyed signal distinguishes published versions from their unreleased originals under the evaluated key-preserving benign transformations. Doctor Trigger complements provenance metadata with release-specific face verification and record-linked evidence for further assessment.

title: Clinical value claims in multimodal AI outpace supporting evidence
summary: Multimodal prediction models add a data source, such as imaging or an assay, to clinical information, and health systems must decide whether that added test is worth acquiring. We audited 177 studies comparing multimodal with unimodal models: 81 from a systematic review and 96 from a probability sample of 2025-2026 PubMed records. Gains in the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) were smaller when a study fitted a separate model for every data source (adjusted difference, -0.030; 95% CI, -0.056 to -0.005). Within 78 such studies, leaving out the strongest source's model would have raised the average gain from 0.046 to 0.108. This complete benchmarking fell from 69.1% of review studies to an estimated 46.0% of recent ones. An estimated 22% assessed decision utility and none evaluated a model prospectively, yet most claimed potential clinical usefulness or improved care (84.0% and an estimated 87.7%).

title: RetinaSC: Retinal Semantic Communication Framework for Diabetic Retinopathy Detection
summary: This paper presents a lightweight semantic com- munication framework for diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading from fundus images pertaining specifically to the APTOS2019 dataset. The framework includes semantic encoder designed using ResNet34, U-Net, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNet-B0 architectures. Further, the trained models are used to train the same framework for IDRiD dataset using transfer learning approach. Such a framework will enable the telemedicine sector in the early detection of DR and prevent total blindness. The results reveal that for APTOS, task-oriented semantic systems can achieve satisfactory robust performance (more than 0.8 weighted F1 score for ResNet34 and EfficientNet-B0) across different channels. In particular, considering the trade-off between complexity, latency, throughput, and F1 score, MobileNetV2 is the best model with weighted F1 score of 0.76-0.78 for both task and reconstruction- oriented modules and end-to-end latency of only 8.162 ms.

title: Routing Optimality for Demand Graphs of Matching Number at Most Two
comment: This paper has been submitted to ITW 2027
summary: We prove that network coding and fractional routing have the same capacity region in undirected networks whose demand graph has matching number at most two, that is, when no three demand edges have pairwise disjoint endpoints. The metric-packing reduction of Liu et al. reduces this problem to a distance-weighted communication inequality on the fixed graph $Γ_{3,3}$. We first prove two entropy inequalities for sessions between designated terminal pairs on $Γ_{3,3}$. We then extend this result to sessions with arbitrary endpoints to obtain the distance-weighted communication bound required by the reduction. The proof combines conditional entropy inequalities with two graph contractions and an information inequality for deterministic interaction. Combining this inequality with the existing reduction establishes routing optimality for this class of demand graphs.

title: Preliminary Exploration of Large Models Based on Self-Supervised Learning for Health Monitoring of Power Electronic Converters
comment: Accepted by Proceedings of the 2nd Electrical Artificial Intelligence Conference, EAIC 2025
summary: Current artificial intelligence (AI) methods for power electronics converters make limited use of the abundant unlabeled data generated during real-world operation. This underexplored resource holds significant potential for advancing model performance. To address this gap, this paper presents PE-TSFM, a time-series foundation model tailored for power module health monitoring. The model adopts the PatchTST architecture combined with self-supervised learning and is trained on more than 143 million timestamps, where over 98\% of this training data is unlabeled and collected directly from an operating traction converter. In degradation classification tasks, PE-TSFM achieves an accuracy of 87\%, considerably surpassing five conventional time-series AI models whose performance ranges from 27\% to 45\%. These results demonstrate the model's strong few-shot learning capability and generalization across different operating conditions. This work promotes a shift from narrowly focused models in power electronics toward unified, scalable foundation models that can unlock value from large-scale unlabeled operational data.

title: Resource-constrained Remote Attestation of Smart Meters Using Merkle Trees in a Trusted Execution Environment
summary: Smart meters are pivotal to the functioning of smart grids, as they measure and transmit energy consumption data that includes sensitive information about household energy usage patterns. While this data offers significant financial benefits, it can also reveal detailed insights into residents' daily routines, making the security of smart meters a critical concern. This paper introduces a novel remote attestation method for smart meters that ensures the integrity and privacy of data exchanged between smart meters and central servers while detecting unauthorized tampering. Our approach structures the communication data into a Merkle Tree-a hash data structure that facilitates efficient data integrity and authenticity verification. All operations involved in constructing the Merkle root and hashing critical data are executed in the secure environment of a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) using OP-TEE, thereby maintaining the integrity and security of the smart meter's data. Comparing our experimental results with the related works highlights the superiority of our method in terms of resource efficiency, security robustness, and the feasibility of implementation on smart meters and resource-constrained devices, thereby enhancing the overall security and reliability of smart grid systems.

title: Sparse-TD-JEPA: Improving Zero-Shot Reinforcement Learning With Sparse Latent Task Representations
summary: Successor-feature-based zero-shot reinforcement learning methods pre-train a task encoder and successor-feature predictor on offline, reward-free data, then recover a policy at test time by solving a closed-form linear regression over a small labeled dataset. We identify an underexplored limitation of this approach: when the task encoder produces dense representations, the inferred reward signal becomes diffuse across the state space, reducing the contrast between goal-relevant states and the background and providing a weaker signal for the policy to follow. We address this limitation by introducing an l1 sparsity penalty that concentrates reward-predictive structure into a smaller effective subspace of the task encoder's latent space. The penalty is applied only during training and requires no architectural change or modification to the closed-form inference procedure. We instantiate this approach as Sparse-TD-JEPA, a single-line of code addition based on Temporal-Difference Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (TD-JEPA) that significantly improved its performance in zero-shot reinforcement learning. We evaluate Sparse-TD-JEPA on 65 tasks across the DeepMind Control (DMC) Suite and OGBench, covering locomotion, navigation, trajectory stitching, puzzle solving, and robotic manipulation. Sparse-TD-JEPA improves over TD-JEPA in all 13 domain-level comparisons. On DMC, it increases the average return from 661 +- 6 to 714 +- 3. On OGBench, it increases the average success rate from 38.0 +- 0.8 to 48.4 +- 2.3, with improvements of 13.4-18.0 percentage points on the evaluated antmaze navigation and stitching domains. Overall, Sparse-TD-JEPA achieves the highest mean performance among established zero-shot baselines in nine of the 13 domains. Analysis further shows that sparsity produces a sharper and more task-informative inferred reward landscape.

title: Semantic Edge-Cloud Communication for Real-Time Urban Traffic Digital Twins
comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, accepted to IEEE Global Communications (Globecom) Conference, 2026
summary: Urban traffic systems are becoming increasingly complex, demanding real-time traffic perception, proactive collision prediction, and intelligent management to improve safety and reduce congestion. Although AI-driven traffic management has shown strong promise, its success relies on diverse, high-quality data spanning critical scenarios such as collisions, near-collisions, and traffic rule violations. Digital twins offer a powerful solution by enabling synchronized virtual replicas of physical traffic environments for real-time monitoring, collision prediction, traffic-flow optimization, and diverse realistic scenario generation. However, continuously synchronizing a high-fidelity urban traffic digital twin through edge surveillance cameras requires substantial edge-cloud communication, and transmitting raw video streams leads to severe bandwidth and latency constraints. To overcome this challenge, this paper proposes a semantic communication-based edge-cloud framework for real-time urban traffic digital twin applications. By leveraging edge intelligence to extract and transmit only task-relevant semantic traffic information instead of full video feeds, the proposed framework significantly reduces communication overhead while preserving the essential dynamics needed for accurate real-time digital twin reconstruction. Experimental results demonstrate more than 99% transmission savings and an average trajectory reconstruction error of only 0.12 m, confirming the proposed framework as an effective, scalable, and low-latency solution for AI-enabled urban traffic digital twin applications.

title: Chordal Codes: Code Construction and Efficient Gaussian-Elimination Decoding
comment: This paper has been submitted to ITW 2027
summary: Maximum-likelihood decoding of linear codes over erasure channels can be considered as solving a linear system of a column submatrix of the parity-check matrix. In practice, Gaussian elimination is usually applied, and its computational cost depends on the structure of the matrix, especially the sparsity and the fill-in generated during the elimination. The \emph{chordal graph}, or \emph{triangulated graph}, first introduced by C. Berge, has a so-called \emph{perfect elimination ordering}, indicating that if the primal graph of a matrix is a chordal graph, then there exists a perfect elimination ordering such that a special class of fill-in under Gaussian elimination following this ordering will be avoided. In this paper, we introduce \emph{chordal codes}, i.e., codes equipped with parity-check matrices such that the primal graphs of the parity-check matrices are chordal. We prove that, for a chordal code, the decoding submatrix associated with any erasure pattern retains a chordal primal graph. So, the complexity of chordal elimination (Gaussian elimination following the perfect elimination ordering applied to the chordal code decoding) will be smaller than decoding a random code by Gaussian elimination. Also, we provide an upper bound on the complexity of chordal elimination.

title: Generic Local Identifiability Does Not Imply Generic Global Identifiability in Linear Networks
summary: We give a counterexample to the implication from generic local to generic global identifiability for linear networks with a fixed topology, independently unknown edge coefficients, and selected excited and measured nodes. A six-node network with nine unknown coefficients has exactly two compatible parameter vectors generically. Adding six excited and measured nodes preserves this ambiguity while making the added coefficients directly recoverable. The resulting twelve-node structure has forty-two independent unknown coefficients and zero diagonal. For every positive bound on the largest eigenvalue magnitude, a nonempty open set of parameters has two distinct compatible networks satisfying that bound. This holds for both real and complex coefficients. Other open regions have exactly one admissible solution. The proof uses a rational transformation exchanging the two solutions and a common limiting matrix whose fourth power vanishes. Exact rational-number certificates verify an explicit pair. The construction also extends algebraically when the unknown coordinates are whole rational transfer functions. Genericity in prescribed numerator and denominator coefficient families, and the requirement that every transfer function vanish at infinite frequency, remain separate questions.

title: Risk-aware Road-network Trajectory Synthesis under Local Differential Privacy
summary: Road-network trajectory synthesis under local differential privacy (LDP) enables mobility data analysis without uploading raw trajectories to an untrusted server. Existing locally private trajectory synthesis methods mainly model whole trajectories, point sequences, or grid-level mobility patterns. However, they cannot handle non-uniform privacy risks caused by local road-network and trajectory contexts, such as endpoints, long-stay-associated regions, and low-out-degree branches. They also do not directly protect conditional next-hop choices on road networks, where a user's selected successor may reveal sensitive local movement intentions. To address these challenges, we propose TrajRACE, a locally private synthesis framework for road-network trajectories. TrajRACE uses start, segment-count, and transition reports to represent trajectories. For each transition, it keeps the current road segment as a public aggregation context and perturbs the true successor among legal successors on the client side. It then assigns risk-aware protection strengths to transitions according to local road-network and trajectory contexts. Finally, the server recovers population-level start, segment-count, and conditional transition statistics from heterogeneous privatized reports, and generates synthetic trajectories that follow the public road-network topology. Experiments on three road-network trajectory datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of TrajRACE in improving synthetic-data utility across distributional, query-based, and pattern-level metrics, while providing stronger protection for high-risk local transitions.

title: PotentialEP: Backprop-Free Training of CIFAR-Scale Generative Models via Equilibrium Propagation
comment: Under review at ICLR 2027. Code: github.com/alexgower/EnergyMatchingEqProp
summary: Generating an image with a diffusion or flow-matching model typically involves integrating a velocity field for hundreds of sequential steps. That computation suits a GPU poorly and an analog neuromorphic substrate well, where one fast, low-power physical relaxation could replace the whole sequence. Two things are needed: a generative algorithm whose computation is a relaxation, and a way to train it without backpropagation, whose global gradient transport is hard to realise in analog. Energy Matching supplies the first, sampling by gradient-descent relaxation on a time-independent potential - but obtaining the gradient that descent follows is itself a backward pass, once per integration step. We prove that a predictive coding network with a single linear injection term added to its energy relaxes to a state whose visible layer carries that gradient inherently, with an error that vanishes for small injection strengths. An Energy Matching model trained by backpropagation can therefore be loaded into this network unchanged and sampled by relaxation alone, matching the original model's FID to within 0.04 at CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-32 scale. The network can also be trained without backpropagation: Equilibrium Propagation reproduces backpropagation's parameter updates to a cosine similarity of 0.9998, and training end to end with those updates reaches an FID of 3.64 on unconditional CIFAR-10 against 3.54 for backpropagation. To our knowledge this is the first CIFAR-10 generative model trained with Equilibrium Propagation, and the first at competitive quality by any backpropagation-free rule. This quality does not require group normalisation or attention: an architecture of only convolutions and pointwise nonlinearities, both native to an analog crossbar, reaches an FID of 3.51 when trained by backpropagation.

title: Sequential Change Point Detection for PSK Modulation Switching
comment: 12 Pages, 5 Figures, Online change-point detection for modulation transitions using CUSUM and MOSUM detectors
summary: Transmitters in adaptive communication systems may switch their modulation scheme at an unknown time, and a receiver must detect this switch quickly without raising frequent false alarms. Existing modulation classification methods label a finite block of received data and do not provide stopping rules with controlled false-alarm and delay performance. We study the sequential detection of a switch from one phase shift keying (PSK) scheme to another over an additive white Gaussian noise channel. We build cumulative-sum (CUSUM) and moving-sum (MOSUM) detectors from the log-likelihood ratio and its low-SNR approximation. For a switch from quadrature PSK to binary PSK, we derive the moment-generating function and probability density function of the approximate statistic. We use them to relate the CUSUM threshold to the average run length to false alarm and the worst-case detection delay. For a switch between any two PSK orders, we approximate the vector of overlapping MOSUM statistics as multivariate Gaussian and obtain bounds on both measures. Monte Carlo simulations show that our derived expressions for ARL2FA and WADD closely match the empirical results across thresholds, validating the accuracy of the proposed analytical approximations and theoretical bounds.

title: Latency-Aware Uplink NOMA-MEC with PASS: A Feasibility-First Resource Allocation Framework
comment: 6 pages, Accepted at IEEE GLOBECOM 2026 Workshops (PASS for NGWC)
summary: Meeting hard task-completion deadlines for many simultaneously offloading users is the binding challenge in mobile-edge computing (MEC). As the user count grows, the transmit power required to satisfy every deadline within per-user budgets rises until no feasible allocation exists. We take a \emph{feasibility-first} view of this $K$-user problem in an uplink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) MEC system served by a pinching-antenna system (PASS), whose radiating points establish strong line-of-sight (LoS) links that lower the received-power requirement. We formulate a latency-constrained joint optimization of transmit powers, CPU frequencies, and antenna configuration. We then derive a \emph{closed-form least-power feasibility test}: the componentwise-least allocation meeting every deadline. It certifies feasibility with the largest attainable margin to the power budgets and defines a practical \emph{quality-of-service (QoS)-feasibility outage} metric, the probability that no allocation meets all deadlines within budget. We solve the problem with a three-block alternating-optimization algorithm that is provably monotone-convergent and has polynomial complexity. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme sustains deadline feasibility at user loads where equal-power, orthogonal multiple access (OMA), and single-antenna baselines fail or degrade sharply, each by a mechanism predicted directly from the system model, whereas the proposed design degrades gracefully. Stress tests further show that feasibility is sustained under order-of-magnitude budget reductions, and that the pinching-antenna array itself enables constrained-budget operation. The result is a scalable, closed-form-initialized design for deadline-feasible offloading.
